item.title: Where is it going wrong for Carrick's Man Utd?
item.description: Thursday marks five months exactly since Man Utd announced Michael Carrick would be staying on as head coach. There will be little mood for celebrating anniversaries the morning after his worst night in the role.

item.title: Carra: Fernandes comments 'disgraceful', but Carrick's time may be up
item.description: Jamie Carragher has criticised Bruno Fernandes for questioning Man Utd's tactics following their 4-1 defeat to Como, but believes that it could be the end of the line for Michael Carrick.

item.title: Kalu mourns late Afenifere leader, Fasoranti
item.description: Former Abia State Governor and Senator representing Abia North, Orji Uzor Kalu, has expressed condolences to the family of late elder statesman and Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, who died at the age of 100. Kalu described the late Yoruba leader as a respected statesman who devoted much of his life to the service of humanity, national unity and Nigeria’s development. In a statement he signed on Tuesday, the senator said Fasoranti lived a long and fulfilled life marked by patriotism, selfless service and commitment to democratic ideals. “Pa Fasoranti lived a long and fulfilled life marked by patriotism, selfless service and commitment to the unity and progress of Nigeria. “His contributions to democracy, good governance and national development will remain part of his enduring legacy,” Kalu said. The former governor extended his condolences to the deceased’s family, the leadership of Afenifere, the government and people of Ondo State, and the Yoruba nation. He urged the family to take solace in Fasoranti’s remarkable life and enduring contributions to the country. Kalu also prayed for the peaceful repose of the late elder statesman’s soul and asked God to grant his family the strength to bear the loss. The post Kalu mourns late Afenifere leader, Fasoranti appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Angel Reese’s confidence is overflowing in powerful message after Dream’s Game 3 win
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Angel Reese’s confidence is overflowing in powerful message after Dream’s Game 3 win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . ATLANTA – Sometimes, it’s just about who wants it more. After letting Game 1 slip through their hands, the Atlanta Dream have responded in the best way possible, and it’s started with Angel Reese herself. In Game 2, her relentlessness and determination to will the team to a victory worked. Whatever high she was on from that game carried over to Atlanta, and it once again helped the Dream to a 97-71 win against the Golden State Valkyries to put them up 2-1 in the series. At this point, it feels like the Dream go when Reese goes, and that’s no problem for her since she sees what it does for them. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “No matter if my shots are falling, I just want to make sure I bring energy,” Reese said after the game. “I just want to be able to come in every day, pour into everybody, bring the energy, bring the morale, because I think it’s contagious. “When you have a mentality that, starting for me, I’m hyped all the time, and I bring the confidence to everyone, y’all not taking this from us. And that’s in my heart. I’m not letting you take this from us, and it becomes contagious within the team. They feel that confidence too. That’s kind of been my mindset throughout the entire season, just being able to want it more than anybody else.” There’s no doubt that the Dream felt it, and it all started in the first quarter. As much as Reese set the tone, she had help from Naz Hillmon, who hit back-to-back 3-pointers in the first. “I think our 3s were huge,” Hillmon said. “Very timely. But I think it also helped to open up our teammates. We’re knocking them down; you can’t continue to help into the paint, bring two to Angel, Rhyne [Howard] or Lish [Gray]. Definitely opened up things that we’ve been working on all year long, and it was nice to see them fall tonight.” Though the Dream were up as much as 12 points in the second quarter, the Valkyries made their run. item.title: Travis Kelce injury update raises fresh concern ahead of Chiefs-Seahawks clash
item.description: Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images Travis Kelce has been listed as limited in practice by the Kansas City Chiefs after suffering an ankle injury during their win over the Los Angeles Chargers, raising a small concern ahead of their clash with the Seattle Seahawks. The veteran tight end picked up the injury in the first quarter of the 22-6 victory but returned to finish the game with four catches for 53 yards. Andy Reid had offered an encouraging update after the win, saying Kelce would be “OK”. However, his limited participation in practice suggests the Chiefs will need to monitor his condition. Travis Kelce’s ankle injury creates concern for Kansas City Chiefs ahead of Seattle Seahawks game Kelce was listed as limited in the Chiefs’ first practice report following the injury. While that does not necessarily mean he is in danger of missing the Seahawks game, it is a development worth watching as the week progresses. Reid previously explained that the 37-year-old had “tweaked” his ankle and expected it to be sore the following day. The fact that Kelce was able to return against the Chargers remains a positive sign for Kansas City. However, with the tight end still being restricted in practice several days later, the team will want to see how he responds before making any decisions about his availability. Kelce is particularly important to the Chiefs given their growing injury problems at receiver. Rashee Rice, who has missed the past two games with a hamstring injury, did not practice. Rookie Cyrus Allen, meanwhile, participated fully despite dealing with a knee issue. Kansas City’s problems also extend to the offensive line, with starting tackles Josh Simmons and Jaylon Moore both missing practice. Tyquan Thornton is another significant absence, with the receiver expected to miss most, if not all, of the remainder of the regular season after suffering a dislocated ankle in Week 3. Losing Kelce as well would leave Patrick Mahomes with even fewer established options in the passing game against the reigning Super Bowl champions. For now, there is no confirmation that Kelce will miss the game. His practice participation over the coming days should provide a clearer indication of whether the ankle injury is likely to affect his availability. The Chiefs will be hoping their veteran tight end can return to full practice and avoid another setback as they prepare for a challenging test against Seattle. item.title: Valkyries fans find community at Rikki's, but not a win in Game 3 of WNBA Finals
item.description: Imogen Doumani, left, and Brooke Peters watch the Golden State Valkyries play the Atlanta Dream during the WNBA Finals at Rikki's Bar in San Francisco on Monday. (Weston Turtle Fudge/S.F. Chronicle) There was no violet wave, no chants of "GSV GSV," and little to cheer for, except for a brief flurry of baskets that tied the game in the third quarter. After that it was all Atlanta Dream, who blew out the Golden State Valkyries by 26 points in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday night . Yet Rikki's on Market Street was packed and cacophonous, again living up to its growing reputation as the micro-Ballhalla satellite in the Castro, the San Francisco women's sports bar the city maybe didn't know it needed and now wonders why it took so long. Most sports bars develop gradually as sports teams catch the imagination of the fan base. Rikki's opened around the Valkyries first game, a low-key neighborhood expression of what would soon become the country's first women's professional sports team with a $1 billion valuation. It has been a pulse of the team's obsessive fans ever since. On Wednesday some of those fans started lining up two hours before the game. While the contest was a blowout - Golden State tied the game twice but never had the lead - fans seemed upbeat and hopeful until the fourth quarter. First in line at Rikki's on Wednesday afternoon were Kevin Smith, Bruna Burns and Adrea Suess, who arrived at 2 p.m., 90 minutes before the bar opened to make sure they got a good table. The trio had been there for the previous game in the series, when Golden State team officials were there to hand out T-shirts to everyone who showed up. "The ambiance is incredible here - it feels so electric - we had to come back," said Smith. "Every Valkyries basket is like a goal in soccer." Rikki's opened in June of last year, about three weeks after the Valkyries played their first game. Co-owners Danielle Thoe and Sara Yergovich met playing for the San Francisco Spikes, an LGBTQ+ soccer team, and both found it unfortunate now hard it was to get sports bars and restaurants to show professional women's soccer and basketball games. Before opening Rikki's - the bar is named for Elizabeth "Rikki" Streicher, a lesbian bar owner, LGBTQ+ activist and advocate for queer sports - they would host watch parties at other venues. They raised $425,000 through crowdfunding and another $390,000 in private investment. Thoe said she could not have imagined that the team would make the playoffs in its first year and the WNBA Finals in its second. Lines have been down the block for most of the playoff games, although Wednesday was a bit more subdued. "The weekend games are smashed. People are standing in the street, crowded at the door to watch the game from outside," she said. "The crowds have just gotten bigger and bigger as the season progressed. item.content:encoded: Imogen Doumani, left, and Brooke Peters watch the Golden State Valkyries play the Atlanta Dream during the WNBA Finals at Rikki's Bar in San Francisco on Monday. (Weston Turtle Fudge/S.F. Chronicle) There was no violet wave, no chants of "GSV GSV," and little to cheer for, except for a brief flurry of baskets that tied the game in the third quarter. After that it was all Atlanta Dream, who blew out the Golden State Valkyries by 26 points in Game 3 of the WNBA Finals on Wednesday night . Yet Rikki's on Market Street was packed and cacophonous, again living up to its growing reputation as the micro-Ballhalla satellite in the Castro, the San Francisco women's sports bar the city maybe didn't know it needed and now wonders why it took so long. Most sports bars develop gradually as sports teams catch the imagination of the fan base. Rikki's opened around the Valkyries first game, a low-key neighborhood expression of what would soon become the country's first women's professional sports team with a $1 billion valuation. It has been a pulse of the team's obsessive fans ever since. On Wednesday some of those fans started lining up two hours before the game. While the contest was a blowout - Golden State tied the game twice but never had the lead - fans seemed upbeat and hopeful until the fourth quarter. First in line at Rikki's on Wednesday afternoon were Kevin Smith, Bruna Burns and Adrea Suess, who arrived at 2 p.m., 90 minutes before the bar opened to make sure they got a good table. The trio had been there for the previous game in the series, when Golden State team officials were there to hand out T-shirts to everyone who showed up. "The ambiance is incredible here - it feels so electric - we had to come back," said Smith. "Every Valkyries basket is like a goal in soccer." Rikki's opened in June of last year, about three weeks after the Valkyries played their first game. Co-owners Danielle Thoe and Sara Yergovich met playing for the San Francisco Spikes, an LGBTQ+ soccer team, and both found it unfortunate now hard it was to get sports bars and restaurants to show professional women's soccer and basketball games. Before opening Rikki's - the bar is named for Elizabeth "Rikki" Streicher, a lesbian bar owner, LGBTQ+ activist and advocate for queer sports - they would host watch parties at other venues. They raised $425,000 through crowdfunding and another $390,000 in private investment. Thoe said she could not have imagined that the team would make the playoffs in its first year and the WNBA Finals in its second. Lines have been down the block for most of the playoff games, although Wednesday was a bit more subdued. "The weekend games are smashed. People are standing in the street, crowded at the door to watch the game from outside," she said. "The crowds have just gotten bigger and bigger as the season progressed. We are just trying to thrive amid the chaos." The biggest crowd of the season was on Sunday the weekend of the Pride parade, a testament to the fact that the Valkyries have been embraced by the LGBTQ community even as the San Francisco Giants earned criticism for their handling of several players who refused to wear or defaced their Pride hats for the Giants' celebration of Pride. Mikey Boothe, who works as a bartender at Chase Center, said he was never much of a sports fan until he discovered the Valkyries, which he called "incredibly inclusive." "I like the Valkyries fans better than the Warriors fans," he said. "They tip better and they are nicer." Molly Lori, a Spanish teacher in San Francisco at International School, has become a regular at the sports bar, stopping by to watch women's soccer and basketball. She said the Valkyries have taken off at school with more students recently sporting Valkyries gear than Warriors. "Someone is doing a really good job with the marketing," she said. "The fashion is unbelievable. Definitely a lot more sequins than you would see at a typical sporting event. The excitement for the Valkyries, you can feel it." Several of those in attendance said they wished that professional women's sports had not taken so long to develop. "When my daughter was playing sports in middle school and high school there was never a option of ‘maybe I'll go pro someday.' It was ‘maybe I'll coach, maybe I'll teach gym,'" said Oakland resident Kay Sirota. "It would have been nice to have. Someday maybe my grandkids will go pro and I'll be the Nana up in the stands, yelling my head off." Anu Bhat, who grew up in India, said she wanted to play basketball as a school-aged girl "but they said there was nobody to coach us." "There was a lack of encouragement and nobody seemed interested in letting girls play," she said. While there may be more demand to watch the games in a bar when the Valkyries are on the road, the atmosphere may be even more passionate at home playoff games, Thoe said. The team will be back at the Chase Center on Monday for Game 5. Rikki's will likely be pulsating with energy - and hopefully the team will get its groove back, she said. "During home games it's more people who choose not to pay the ticket prices or can't afford to pay," she said. "It's a little more of a special, a little more of a community feeling." item.title: Justin Faulk trade destinations after being named Red Wings trade candidate
item.description: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Justin Faulk trade destinations after being named Red Wings trade candidate appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Red Wings are going through a bit of a rough patch at this time. Detroit has two ongoing trade requests on the table: Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson. Larkin recently expanded his trade list , while there isn’t a ton known about Edvinsson at this time. The Red Wings are also struggling at the start of the 2026-27 campaign . Detroit is last place in one of the strongest divisions in all of hockey. They have gutted out some games to earn a few overtime-loss points. Still, the Red Wings are last in the Atlantic. It does not appear as if this team is going to make a ton of strides this season. A lot of people in the hockey world are wondering what will happen with Larkin and Edvinsson. However, there is another player popping up in trade conversations. The Athletic put together a list of potential trade candidates from all 32 teams. They named defenseman Justin Faulk as one to watch for Detroit. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The Red Wings are at the bottom of a loaded Atlantic Division, they have two young righties ready to play in Axel Sandin-Pellikka and camp surprise Anton Johansson, and Faulk is a pending UFA. It’s not under the radar in Detroit, but he’s a name to watch this season,” Red Wings beat writer Max Bultman said of Faulk. With this in mind, let’s take a look at two potential destinations for the veteran defenseman early in the 2026-27 NHL season. Bruins still need defensive upgrades Thomas Salus-Imagn Images The Boston Bruins made some big moves in the offseason to bolster their defensive core. Boston traded for Will Borgen in a trade with the New York Rangers in July. They also re-signed Connor Clifton in NHL Free Agency after he spent a bit of time elsewhere. Despite the moves made, Boston is still leaking shots against. Goaltender Jeremy Swayman has faced the third-most shots against in the league, according to HockeyStats.com. He is also third in shot attempts faced, as well. Swayman was a big reason the Bruins made the Stanley Cup Playoffs last season. He wasn’t elite, by any means. But he stood on his head when the Bruins needed him to. It appears he’s doing it again early in 2026-27. The Bruins are asking a lot of Swayman to continue facing high shot volumes. Boston has to find ways to limit the pressure he faces. Faulk can block shots, is solid defensively, and has an offensive touch as well. The Red Wings and Bruins have some recent trade history. In fact, their blueline this season is almost the complete opposite of what it was last year. The Ducks made the playoffs with a good mix of veteran talent and exciting young stars. This year, they have just one defenseman (Nick Jensen) older than 27. So far, this young defense has done a decent job limiting shot attempts. Starting goaltender Lukas Dostal has faced the seventh-most shot attempts this year, but only the 15th-most shots on goal. Still, the Ducks could do more. They also could do with another veteran presence on the blueline. This is a rough one for the Red Wings, though. Anaheim doesn’t have the cap space to truly make this work. These teams would need to get creative to make something happen. If they can agree to terms, though, Faulk would be an asset for the Ducks. item.title: Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes criticised manager Michael Carrick’s tactics following the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. United fell behind to a second-minute goal and never recovered as the club’s winless run reached seven games after another lacklustre performance. “We started on the wrong foot and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.” The Portugal midfielder suggested Nico Paz’s early strike for Como on Wednesday night had a damaging effect on the visitors, leaving them struggling to impose themselves. Paz scored again after Tasos Douvikas had doubled the lead, with Jacobo Ramon adding a fourth. Only a stoppage-time goal from Joshua Zirkzee stopped United from succumbing to their joint-heaviest Champions League loss. “Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood of defeat,” said Fernandes. “It’s difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. “If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.” Fernandes also highlighted United’s passive approach out of possession, saying Como were allowed too much time and space to dictate play. Asked whether those comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes said: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me. “Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Fernandes is the latest United player to publicly break ranks. Defender Lisandro Martinez took aim at the club’s hierarchy following a 2-0 Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid last week. Martinez said Carrick had been left with an understrength squad. He later apologised. Youri Tielemans, who started alongside Fernandes in the United midfield in Italy, admitted the display was simply not good enough. “We got outplayed for most of the game so it was a very disappointing night,” said Tielemans. “You can be good tactically but if the effort is not good (then it will not work) and vice versa. You need to be good at everything and tonight we were poor.” AFP The post Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

United fell behind to a second-minute goal and never recovered as the club’s winless run reached seven games after another lacklustre performance. “We started on the wrong foot and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.” The Portugal midfielder suggested Nico Paz’s early strike for Como on Wednesday night had a damaging effect on the visitors, leaving them struggling to impose themselves. item.title: Mavericks’ Cooper Flagg sums up reason Dallas got blown out by Rockets in season opener
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Mavericks’ Cooper Flagg sums up reason Dallas got blown out by Rockets in season opener appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg pointed to poor organization and defensive breakdowns following Wednesday’s 18-point loss to the Houston Rockets. The defeat marked a disappointing beginning to the Mavericks’ new season under head coach Dusty May. Flagg acknowledged that Dallas struggled to respond once Houston built momentum, especially as the Rockets pushed the pace. “We got stagnant,” Flagg said, according to Mike Curtis. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “They obviously went on a run, and we just didn’t have any answers to be more organized.” The second-year forward also highlighted the Mavericks’ inability to recover defensively during Houston’s decisive stretch. “We weren’t getting back in transition,” Flagg admitted. He added that several players departed from their usual habits as the game slipped away. “People were doing things that they don’t normally do & it really showed.” Flagg’s assessment suggested that Dallas’ problems extended beyond missed shots or individual performances. Instead, the Mavericks struggled to maintain their offensive structure and let Houston capitalize on mistakes. Those issues proved costly against a Rockets team featuring Kevin Durant, who delivered an emphatic dunk over Flagg during the contest. The play involving Durant and Flagg provided another memorable moment in Houston’s opening-night victory. For Dallas, the result raises immediate questions about execution and consistency under its new coaching staff. Flagg’s comments also reflected the importance of staying disciplined when opponents build momentum. The Mavericks must now address their transition defense and offensive decision-making before their next matchup. Their season-opening defeat demonstrated how quickly a competitive game can unravel when communication and organization break down. Related: Kyrie Irving flashes vintage form on 1st NBA bucket in almost 600 days Related: Mavericks sign 2025 Jazz first round pick to two-way contract

And we’re not even at Halloween yet! We have to be fluid, though, because the roster we look at and feel good about on Thursday night could look completely different by Saturday. I’m incredibly excited to bring this article to all of you this season and hope you enjoy the ride. If you have any questions, feel free to find me on Bluesky (@ktompkinsii.bsky.social). Tag me in a post with any lineup questions, and I’ll do my best to answer them. Let’s get into it! All game and implied point totals listed were compiled via DraftKings Sportsbook on Tuesday for NE-CHI, PIT-NO, SF-ATL, CLE-TEN and IND-MIN. Teams on bye in Week 6: Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers and Washington Commanders. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears Favorite: Bears –3 Game Total: 50.5 Implied Point Total: Bears 26.75, Patriots 23.75 Patriots Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: QB Drake Maye Patriots RBs TreVeyon Henderson suffered a high ankle sprain last week. Conventional wisdom suggested that Hendo would miss Week 6. Not so fast! Henderson ended up playing, though he had a reduced workload, with just seven carries for 31 yards. We also assumed Rhamondre Stevenson would handle most of the work. He was on the field more than any other back, playing 60% of snaps and running routes on 46% of dropbacks. He took just 39% of the team’s rushing attempts but still led the backfield in touches, with 14 carries for only 36 yards. Corey Kiner ended up taking 11 carries himself, starting in the third quarter and playing well into the fourth against the Jets. New England led by less than a touchdown for much of that stretch and never by more than 10 points. These were meaningful carries in a game that remained undecided. Still, it was disappointing that Stevenson couldn’t handle the full workload. One would assume that, with Stevenson and Henderson fully healthy, they would take virtually all the touches available to running backs. However, the Patriots’ decision to add Kiner shows that he could remain an annoying obstacle, taking touches away from both backs even when they’re healthy. Fantasy Advice: Kiner’s greater-than-anticipated involvement makes this backfield murky and drags Stevenson and Henderson down to flex-level fantasy options against the Bears. WR A.J. Brown Designated to return from injured reserve in the middle of last week, Brown made his return to the Patriots’ lineup in Week 6 against the Jets and promptly led New England’s pass-catchers in targets (nine). However, he didn’t look like himself in the Patriots’ win. Brown caught only three balls for 27 yards and ran routes on 97% of Drake Maye ’s dropbacks in a game marred by drops and inconsistency. Brown had a gift-wrapped long touchdown catch in the second quarter, but the ball slipped through his hands. Maybe it was because of his lengthy layoff? Either way, with a full week of practice and this game under his belt, Brown will be needed now more than ever with Romeo Doubs hitting IR after hurting his shoulder on his 42-yard touchdown grab in Week 6. Fantasy Advice: While Brown’s first game back was disappointing, he remains a WR2 option and will be relied upon against the Bears, a below-average team in fantasy points allowed to wide receivers this season. Patriots WRs Doubs’ only catch of the game was his 42-yard touchdown. With Brown’s lackluster performance, Demario Douglas picked up the slack, finishing with a team-leading seven receptions for 86 yards and a touchdown. Douglas ran the second-most routes on the team, mostly from the slot, and will be relied upon with Doubs on the shelf. On the outside, it’ll be some combination of Efton Chism III (one target, no catches and a 29% route rate) and Kyle Williams (one target, one catch for 12 yards and a 60% route rate) without Doubs for at least the next few games. Fantasy Advice: Without Doubs, Douglas gets a bump up to a high-end flex play, as Brown will need somebody else to help earn targets. Douglas is the best option for that role. Keep an eye on Chism and Williams, but neither is worth adding outside of super-deep fantasy leagues on a short week. Bears Fantasy Notes Must-Start Players: None QB Caleb Williams Returning to the Bears’ lineup for his first game action since Week 2, Williams was incredibly efficient, completing 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. Given his previous hamstring ailment, it was expected that he wouldn’t run much in his return, and he managed only three rushing yards. With a solid foundation to build on with his pass-catchers, Williams was a fringe QB1 despite throwing just one touchdown. Fantasy Advice: Against the Patriots on a short week, Williams is a solid QB1 option with considerable upside on Thursday Night Football. Bears RBs Things are trending toward a D’Andre Swift / Roschon Johnson week on a short turnaround for Thursday night against the Patriots. With Kyle Monangai (toe) out for a second straight week, both Swift and Johnson saw plenty of touches, with 20 for Swift and 15 for Johnson. Swift scored twice on the ground and added four receptions for 26 yards, but posted –35 RYOE, dead last among 38 qualifying RBs. Johnson was marginally better and added a rushing score of his own. It’s a fruitful backfield for fantasy production, so at least there’s that! Fantasy Advice: The split will probably remain similar on a short week, so with Monangai out, Johnson becomes a sneaky flex option. Swift is a fine RB2 for the matchup against New England, which has a middle-of-the-road defense when it comes to preventing fantasy scoring from running backs. WR Luther Burden III While Burden III led the Bears across the board with a team-leading eight targets and eight receptions for 95 yards, the main takeaway is a percentage: 44%. That was Burden’s route participation rate in Week 6, a season low by a wide margin. Burden still earned those targets on such limited route volume, but if that continues, it’s a glaring signal to opposing defenses: “Hey, Burden is on the field, so he’s getting the ball!” The fact that Burden still led the team in targets per route run (TPRR) at 44% and first-read target share at 31.6% is remarkable. Let’s hope the route participation issue was just a minor weekly glitch. Fantasy Advice: For Week 7 at home against the Patriots, Burden is a low-end WR3 with obvious upside in a good matchup. He likely won’t have to match up against New England’s star cornerback Christian Gonzalez. WR Rome Odunze Odunze led Chicago in route participation at 98%, but he certain

item.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic sounds off on making Yaxel Lendeborg pay for trash talk
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Lakers’ Luka Doncic sounds off on making Yaxel Lendeborg pay for trash talk appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers took care of business in their season opener against the Golden State Warriors , 127-105, at Crypto.com Arena, with the new trio of Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler leading the charge . After a tight contest in the first half, the Lakers outscored the Warriors, 36-16, in the third quarter to make it a one-sided affair. They kept pouring it on and rolled to an easy victory. Doncic had 28 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, and three steals. He admitted that he got fired up by his word war with Yaxel Lendeborg in the second quarter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I think everybody knows when somebody starts talking, you get a different me. So that was it,” said Doncic in the postgame interview. "Everybody knows when somebody starts talking, you get a different me. So that was it.” Luka Doncic when asked about his constant trash talk with Yaxel Lendeborg 🗣️ (via @ESPNNBA ) pic.twitter.com/m3xcaALPvl — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 22, 2026 The six-time All-Star claimed that Lendeborg started the verbal spat. Although Doncic clapped back at the fiery rookie with an expletive remark, he added that he is trying to dial back his on-court vigor. “He was talking crazy. But I wasn’t trying to talk back this season, not trying to get techs. So it was the first time that was not a double-tech because I didn’t say anything. So I’m working on it. But as you see, I think it worked great,” added Doncic in the postgame conference. "It was the first time that was not a double-tech because I didn't say nothing. So I'm working on it." Luka Doncic on his exchange with Yaxel Landeborg at the end of the 1st half 🗣 (via @SpectrumSN ) pic.twitter.com/VpCFxEV3Ry — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 22, 2026 Doncic, the reigning scoring champion, shot 7-of-18 from the field, including 5-of-12 from long range. Lendeborg had 12 points and three rebounds. Reaves tallied 23 points, four rebounds, six assists, and two steals, while Kessler added 26 points on 12-of-12 shooting, nine rebounds, and two blocks. The Lakers will face the Los Angeles Clippers on Friday. Related: Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic Related: Lakers’ Luka Doncic speaks about his future in LA as the face of the franchise

item.title: Walker Kessler delivers in debut as Lakers punish Warriors on opening night
item.description: The Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) passes the ball during an NBA basketball game against The Golden State Warriors on October 21st, 2026 at crypto Arena in Los Angeles, California LOS ANGELES — Walker Kessler had talked about the expectations of playing center for the Los Angeles Lakers. On Wednesday, he finally got to experience it. The nerves came before tipoff. A big Lakers debut followed. Kessler scored 26 points and grabbed nine rebounds in his regular-season Lakers debut, helping L.A. beat the Golden State Warriors 127-105 on opening night. Alongside Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves, he gave the Lakers an immediate look at how productive their new core could be. Dončić finished with a game-high 28 points, seven rebounds and eight assists, while Reaves added 23 points and six assists. The trio’s combined 77 points helped L.A. turn a close first quarter into a comfortable win, with the lead reaching 35 in the fourth. Kessler, Dončić and Reaves supplied 27 of the Lakers’ 34 first-quarter points. That production helped offset Stephen Curry’s fast start, as he scored 16 of Golden State’s first 21 points. Curry scored seven points the rest of the way, finishing with 23 in 21 minutes. THE SWING L.A. led 34-33 after the first quarter before taking control in the second, outscoring Golden State 32-19 to enter halftime ahead 66-52. Dončić helped drive that stretch while trading words with Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. Lendeborg picked up a technical foul and multiple fouls against Dončić, who punctuated the half with a buzzer-beater that brought the crowd to its feet. Dončić followed the basket with more words toward Lendeborg, closing a quarter in which the Lakers established control. Luka Doncic just hit a half court shot and was chirping at rookie Yaxel Lendeborg after. Luka has 23 points as the #Lakers lead it 66-52 at the half. pic.twitter.com/SbTF556Epf — Carlos Yakimowich (@CarlosYakJr) October 22, 2026 The advantage grew to 32 in the third quarter before reaching its largest margin, 35, in the fourth. After Golden State stayed close through the opening period, L.A. created enough separation in the second half to let Dončić rest the entire fourth quarter. THE DIFFERENCE-MAKER Dončić was work class, but Kessler had probably one of the best Lakers debuts we have seen. He finished a perfect 12 for 12 from the field, with 11 baskets coming on dunks, including mostly alley-oop finishes. His production around the rim gave the Lakers a third scoring threat alongside their starting guards. Walker Kessler’s first non-dunk of the night. He had 11 dunks before this. He’s now 12/12 from the floor with 24 points. #Lakers pic.twitter.com/4x2tbqroSk — Carlos Yakimowich (@CarlosYakJr) October 22, 2026 “I definitely was a little nervous going into the game. His debut offered an encouraging first response. “I think it's a big deal when it's your first game as a Laker,” Redick said. “We've had conversations; he understands what this is and the pressures that come with it. I think it was a good opening statement for him.” For a core that shared limited time together during the preseason, Kessler’s efficient finishing provided something to build on. “That's just the first game,” Dončić said. “I think our ceiling is even higher.” Important Notes Ziaire Williams and Matisse Thybulle starting alongside Dončić, Reaves and Kessler. Quentin Grimes and Sandro Mamukelashvili were the notable first substitutes of the game. Jake LaRavia rolled his ankle in the fourth quarter and remained down in pain before receiving assistance. He later walked to the locker room under his own power. There is no update on his injury. WHERE THEY STAND The Lakers opened the season 1-0 to start the new era with tons of excitement surrounding this new-look team. UP NEXT The Lakers host the Los Angeles Clippers on Friday for Game 2 of the season.

item.title: Walker Kessler left in awe by Shaq’s message after his Lakers debut
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Walker Kessler left in awe by Shaq’s message after his Lakers debut appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On opening night, new Los Angeles Lakers starting center Walker Kessler stood tall and took advantage of a matchup against the small Golden State Warriors — proving himself to be well worth thus far of the $130 million the team splashed on him. In his debut for the Purple and Gold, Kessler recorded 26 points and nine rebounds, and he shot the ball perfectly from the field — making all 12 of his field-goal attempts on the night to help power LA to a 127-105 victory. Kessler also added two blocks for good measure, and he immediately showed why the Lakers made a concerted effort to sign him in free agency. After the game, the Lakers’ new starting center received some love from a legend of the franchise in Shaquille O’Neal, who showered him with praise after his statement game against the Dubs. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The way you played tonight you played like the best big man in the league. I’m happy for you, I’m proud of you. Welcome to the big man alliance. I love you brother. Continue to play well,” O’Neal said on ESPN’s Inside The NBA, via Oh No He Didn’t on X. Shaq giving Walker Kessler his flowers: "The way you played tonight you played like the best big man in the league. I'm happy for you, I'm proud of you. Welcome to the big man alliance. I love you brother. And I want you to guys to love the name Snowtime (Lakers)" https://t.co/cuCDJbPTlF pic.twitter.com/Qkis8iQKcc — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) October 22, 2026 Kessler knows just how high O’Neal’s standards can be for a center, so he was left in awe after hearing that kind of commendation. “That means so much coming from you, Shaq,” Kessler added. The Lakers invested a significant amount of money and draft picks to bring Kessler in via a sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz to address their well-known need for a long-term solution at the five. Kessler was coming off a season in which he played just five games for the Jazz after he underwent season-ending shoulder surgery, so acquiring him did not come without risk for the Lakers. But it has become evident quickly how impactful Kessler can be for this team when he’s at his best. He will look to keep this going when the Lakers host the Los Angeles Clippers on Friday for their second game of the 2026-27 season. Related: Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic Related: Lakers’ Luka Doncic speaks about his future in LA as the face of the franchise

item.title: Court warns defence against delay in trial of 4 suspects over DSS officer’s murder
item.description: * Adjourns to 28 October The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday warned the defence lawyers against delay in the trial of four suspects who allegedly kidnapped and killed Ekpeyong Asuquo Owoh, an operative of the Department of State Services (DSS). Justice Joyce Abdulmalik gave the warning after Kelvin Ekwe and Geoffrey Uwadiegu, who appeared for the defendants, expressed unreadiness to commence trial and sought an application for adjournment. When the case was called, Munirat Oladunjoye, who represented the prosecution, informed the court that the matter was fixed for trial following the defendants’ denial of the allegations. She, however, told the court that the prosecution had an application to shield the identity of their witnesses pursuant to Section 232(3)(b) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA), 2015. Oladunjoye, therefore, prayed the court for an order granting the permission to mask their witnesses and not to reveal their names. But lawyer to the 1st and 2nd defendants, Kelvin Ekwe, disagreed with Oladunjoye’s oral application. He argued that such application was uncalled for. Ekwe submitted that from the proof of evidence served on them, only a witness was listed as DSS investigation officer. According to him, there is no evidence that if the witnesses are not masked, it will prejudice the prosecution’s case. Besides, he argued that the application should be formally filed for them to respond appropriately and to guard against ambush. Justice Abdulmalik then asked Ekwe to cite any law to back his argument that the prosecution must file a formal application to make such request. Responding, the lawyer said he relied on Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution. Oladunjoye also countered Ekwe’s submission. In a short ruling, the judge agreed with the DSS lawyer’s submission. Justice Abdulmalik held that in the light that the case being a terrorism matter, it would not serve the interest of justice to expose the identity of the witnesses in the case. The judge, who directed the trial to commence and the witness to be co-named as “AB”, ordered that anyone who runs foul of Section 232(5) of ACJA will be liable to one year jail term. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: * Adjourns to 28 October The Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday warned the defence lawyers against delay in the trial of four suspects who allegedly kidnapped and killed Ekpeyong Asuquo Owoh, an operative of the Department of State Services (DSS). Justice Joyce Abdulmalik gave the warning after Kelvin Ekwe and Geoffrey Uwadiegu, who appeared for the defendants, expressed unreadiness to commence trial and sought an application for adjournment. When the case was called, Munirat Oladunjoye, who represented the prosecution, informed the court that the matter was fixed for trial following the defendants’ denial of the allegations. She, however, told the court that the prosecution had an application to shield the identity of their witnesses pursuant to Section 232(3)(b) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA), 2015. Oladunjoye, therefore, prayed the court for an order granting the permission to mask their witnesses and not to reveal their names. But lawyer to the 1st and 2nd defendants, Kelvin Ekwe, disagreed with Oladunjoye’s oral application. He argued that such application was uncalled for. Ekwe submitted that from the proof of evidence served on them, only a witness was listed as DSS investigation officer. According to him, there is no evidence that if the witnesses are not masked, it will prejudice the prosecution’s case. Besides, he argued that the application should be formally filed for them to respond appropriately and to guard against ambush. Justice Abdulmalik then asked Ekwe to cite any law to back his argument that the prosecution must file a formal application to make such request. Responding, the lawyer said he relied on Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution. Oladunjoye also countered Ekwe’s submission. In a short ruling, the judge agreed with the DSS lawyer’s submission. Justice Abdulmalik held that in the light that the case being a terrorism matter, it would not serve the interest of justice to expose the identity of the witnesses in the case. The judge, who directed the trial to commence and the witness to be co-named as “AB”, ordered that anyone who runs foul of Section 232(5) of ACJA will be liable to one year jail term. Geoffrey Uwadiegwu, counsel to the 3rd and 4th defendants, informed the court that he was coming into the matter for the first and and that he would need more time to study the case file. Ekwe also told the court that he was just served with the video evidence by the prosecution, insisting that he was not ready to go on with the trial. The prosecution lawyer responded that though Ekwe was just being served with the video evidence, the video clip would not be used in today’s trial. She prayed the court to allow the matter to proceed. Oladunjoye argued that Ekwe’s absence on October 6 caused the case to be adjourned. Dissatisfied, Ekwe and Uwadiegwu stood up at the same time to address court on why the matter must be adjourned. But the judge cautioned them against unruly behaviour in her court. “I run my court in line with international best practice, and that is why people say I am strict. “So, when I run my court, there should be 99.9 per cent compliance according to international best practice,” she said. Justice Abdulmalik said she wouldn’t have listed the case for hearing because there were many pre-election cases in the docket of the court. She added that she had at least nine judgments to write in respect of pre-election matters which must be delivered before Nov. 9. The judge, however, said that she saw the case as very crucial and which should be determined expeditiously. Having listened to the parties, Justice Abdulmalik agreed to give a short adjournment. She, however, warned against any act that could delay the trial. The judge consequently adjourned the matter until 28 October at the instance of the two defence lawyers. Suspects The suspects, Michael Okafor, a.k.a Onyechimeleze; Chinedu Chukwudozie, alias Kante; Chibunna Olisa; and Chigozie Olisa, a.k.a Ability were arraigned before Justice Abdulmalik on 28 September on a six-count charge bordering on terrorism and kidnapping. The prosecution alleged that the defendants conspired to commit acts of terrorism and were involved in the abduction of Owoh, while he was travelling from Port Harcourt in Rivers to Awka in Anambra. They were further accused of taking the operative hostage and causing his death in the course of the alleged criminal operation. The suspects were also accused of belonging to the proscribed IPOB and its armed wing, the Eastern Security Network (ESN), as well as involvement in activities allegedly linked to terrorism. In addition, the prosecution alleged that the suspects were involved in the unlawful possession of firearms, including AK-47 and pump-action rifles, in connection with the alleged offences. The charges followed investigations into the circumstances surrounding the abduction and killing of the officer and the alleged activities of the defendants. item.title: Cardinals star Jeremiyah Love’s status for Broncos game in doubt after practice absence
item.description: Patrick Breen/The Republic / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Cardinals star Jeremiyah Love’s status for Broncos game in doubt after practice absence appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals are coming off an incredible high. Amid their turbulent 2026 season, Arizona was able to snag a win against one of the best teams in the league on paper. Their 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams this past Sunday was an incredible morale-boosting win for the squad. They did that even without one of their best players; running back Jeremiyah Love was injured and did not play last week. Fans are perhaps hoping that Love will return to the field this week when the Cardinals take on the Denver Broncos, a much tougher defense. However, the first day of this week’s practice does not bode well for the team. Love was absent from Wednesday’s practice session : a troubling sign for the star’s availability in Week 7. Wednesday’s injury report for Cardinals-Broncos. pic.twitter.com/bG65Y31zrV Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Josh Weinfuss (@joshweinfuss) October 21, 2026 Love was out for the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams due to an ankle injury he got the week prior . Without Love, the Cardinals had to rely on Zonovan Knight and Tyler Allegier. Allegier was rather quiet in the win (38 yards on 10 carries), but Knight was electric in the game. Nicknamed “Bam,” the running back notched 80 yards on 15 carries. He constantly gashed the Rams’ defense with big runs that set the Cardinals up in good field position. While the offense never scored a touchdown, it was able to record six field goals. That, apparently, was enough to hold off the Rams’ attack. The Cardinals were able to do just enough to keep away from their division rivals, especially on defense. However, it’s also clear that the Cardinals need to have Love back to add another gear to their offense. There will be two more days before Love makes his return to the field. If he doesn’t participate or is limited in any capacity… he’s likely not going to play a single snap in Week 7. Related: Bears’ perfect Josh Sweat trade offer to Cardinals before NFL trade deadline Related: Cowboys’ perfect Josh Sweat trade offer to Cardinals before NFL trade deadline

item.title: NIMASA detains four vessels over Cabotage breaches
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) has intensified enforcement of the Cabotage regime, detaining vessels found to have violated the country’s coastal shipping regulations as part of efforts to ensure compliance with local content requirements in the maritime sector. The operation which focused on vessels of interest identified through intelligence and surveillance profiling led to the arrest and detention of several vessels for nonconformity including MT HOLMES, MT FUJAIRAH ENERGY, JS GRATITUDE, MT BORA within the Lagos maritime domain. Some of the vessels which have regularised their infractions have since been release. Operation Sea Guardian was conducted as a follow-up enforcement initiative aimed at strengthening regulatory compliance, verifying cabotage obligations, assessing surcharge and levy compliance, and ensuring adherence to applicable maritime regulations. It deployed Deep Blue assets to help track, board, inspect, and verify the operational status of vessels identified through intelligence reports and compliance indicators through effective inter-agency cooperation among NIMASA enforcement personnel, the Nigerian Navy, the Maritime Guard Command and C4i intelligence personnel. Reacting to the development, the Director General of NIMASA, Dr. Dayo Mobereola emphasised that such operations are going to be more frequent and that defaulting operators would face the full wrath of the law. According to him, “we had earlier served notice of enhanced enforcement of indigenous participation in our coastal and inland trade and this is exactly what we are doing. It is therefore in the interest of operators to ensure total compliance because defaulters will be visited with stiff sanctions in line with the law”. The post NIMASA detains four vessels over Cabotage breaches appeared first on Vanguard News .

There is an obvious edge to the fixture. The last time these sides met, India beat New Zealand by 96 runs in the T20 World Cup final in March, and Mitchell Santner's team will not have forgotten how comprehensively that night went against them. item.title: Lewis Steele: Blockbuster new Liverpool contract should be ‘a matter of when, not if’
item.description: Lewis Steele: Blockbuster new Liverpool contract should be ‘a matter of when, not if’ Lewis Steele believes that a new contract at Liverpool for Rio Ngumoha will be a matter of when and not if, with the player seemingly determined to remain at Anfield for the long-term. The 18-year-old was simply outstanding in the Champions League win over Villarreal on Tuesday night, putting in the kind of performance which’ll have European giants on alert for any potential fractures in his relationship with the Reds. His current deal runs to June 2028, and Fabrizio Romano indicated over the past couple of days that ‘active conversations’ are ongoing over a prospective extension which’d keep him on Merseyside for another while yet. Steele addresses Ngumoha contract question In a Liverpool Confidential Q&A for the Daily Mail , Steele was asked if he had an update on Ngumoha’s contract situation, replying: ‘The 18-year-old’s agent is in talks with Liverpool over renewing his contract and there is no reason for fans to worry. ‘Ngumoha is on course to extend his deal (which currently runs until 2028) and, as revealed in Confidential a month ago, sources close to the player have told us he loves the club and wants to commit his long-term future. ‘It would seem a matter of ‘when’ not ‘if’ despite interest from Arsenal, Bayern Munich and other European clubs.’ (Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images) All the signs point towards Ngumoha signing a new deal With both Romano and Steele claiming that Ngumoha and Liverpool have a mutual desire to extend the winger’s contract, there are definitely positive signs that he’ll renew his commitment to the Reds beyond the summer after next. The teenager is currently on the lower end of the first-team pay scale on £35,000 per week ( Capology ), but any new deal would surely see him increase that substantially to better reflect his importance to Andoni Iraola’s side. Crucially, the 18-year-old is enjoying plenty of game-time at Anfield, featuring in nine of our 11 matches so far this season and starting five ( Transfermarkt ). That show of faith will hopefully convince Ngumoha that his head coach firmly believes in him and that he’ll become an automatic starter for Liverpool in time. There hasn’t yet any indication as to how far talks over a new deal have progessed, so speculation could continue for another while yet, but all the signs appear to point towards him penning a bumper new contract in the next few months. If indeed that happens, it’d represent a huge win for Julian Ward in the early part of his reign as LFC sporting director.

item.title: 'It looked like men against kids' - Dimitar Berbatov slams 'terrible' Manchester United display in 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como
item.description: Como 1907 v Manchester United - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Former Manchester United striker Dimitar Berbatov has launched a scathing assessment of his old club following Wednesday's humiliating Champions League thrashing away at Como. The Bulgarian pundit questioned the players' effort as Cesc Fabregas' Serie A outfit dismantled the visitors in torrential rain in Italy. Former striker condemns Italian humiliation Berbatov has tore into his former club's display after they were dismantled 4-1 by Fabregas' side in Wednesday's Champions League encounter . Just eight days after conceding inside the opening minute against Atletico Madrid, the Red Devils were breached after 118 seconds by Nico Paz. That lapse made them the first English club in history to concede inside two minutes across consecutive major European fixtures. 1 - Manchester United are the first English team in history to concede in the first two minutes of consecutive major European matches (1st minute vs Atlético Madrid, 2nd minute vs Como). Downpour. pic.twitter.com/kdErhRxegf — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) October 21, 2026 Rampant hosts expose defensive frailties Como 1907 v Manchester United - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 The Argentine playmaker bagged a brace and teed up Tasos Douvikas in between, before Jacobo Ramon powered home a fourth header for a club that was playing in Serie D when United last lifted the Champions League in 2008. Delivering a damning verdict on how comprehensively the visitors were outclassed when speaking to TNT Sports , Berbatov said: "It was a terrible, terrible night. A terrible game for United, nothing was happening, and Como outplayed them in every way possible. From the goals, from taking the ball, the possession, the confidence. Everything was there for Como." Analysing the hosts' early opener and the space afforded to Paz, he added: "It was like they were playing a second team. Look at the first goal, the confidence on the ball, the time on the ball." Lacklustre effort sparks deeper questions Only a stoppage-time consolation from substitute Joshua Zirkzee via an Amad Diallo cross spared the visitors from matching their heaviest Champions League defeat (a 4-0 loss to Barcelona in 1994) or their worst-ever European reverse (5-0 against Sporting in 1964). Zirkzee had replaced skipper Bruno Fernandes midway through the second half after £110 million-worth of INEOS signings, Matheus Cunha and Andrey Santos, were hooked at the interval. Focusing on the manner of the capitulation rather than the scoreline itself, Berbatov observed: "Sometimes it's not about the loss, it's about how you lose, and today that was the point, how we lost that game of football. After a performance like this, probably, like every time, [people ask], 'Are these the right players to compete on the highest stage? Is that the right manager? Is this the right way?' Downpour. pic.twitter.com/kdErhRxegf — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) October 21, 2026 Rampant hosts expose defensive frailties Como 1907 v Manchester United - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 The Argentine playmaker bagged a brace and teed up Tasos Douvikas in between, before Jacobo Ramon powered home a fourth header for a club that was playing in Serie D when United last lifted the Champions League in 2008. Delivering a damning verdict on how comprehensively the visitors were outclassed when speaking to TNT Sports , Berbatov said: "It was a terrible, terrible night. A terrible game for United, nothing was happening, and Como outplayed them in every way possible. From the goals, from taking the ball, the possession, the confidence. Everything was there for Como." Analysing the hosts' early opener and the space afforded to Paz, he added: "It was like they were playing a second team. Look at the first goal, the confidence on the ball, the time on the ball." Lacklustre effort sparks deeper questions Only a stoppage-time consolation from substitute Joshua Zirkzee via an Amad Diallo cross spared the visitors from matching their heaviest Champions League defeat (a 4-0 loss to Barcelona in 1994) or their worst-ever European reverse (5-0 against Sporting in 1964). Zirkzee had replaced skipper Bruno Fernandes midway through the second half after £110 million-worth of INEOS signings, Matheus Cunha and Andrey Santos, were hooked at the interval. Focusing on the manner of the capitulation rather than the scoreline itself, Berbatov observed: "Sometimes it's not about the loss, it's about how you lose, and today that was the point, how we lost that game of football. After a performance like this, probably, like every time, [people ask], 'Are these the right players to compete on the highest stage? Is that the right manager? Is this the right way?' Of course, after games like this, people will say we need more players, we need better players, we need this and that. What can you say after a performance like this?" Questioning the commitment shown by the squad on the night, the Bulgarian concluded: "Today it didn't look like everyone was giving their best on the pitch. Como looked like they were just having fun. It looked like men against kids." Apologetic manager faces uncertain future imago-sport-1084865974.jpg Wednesday's chastening result piles immense pressure on beleaguered boss Michael Carrick ahead of this weekend's domestic test against Bournemouth. At full-time, the head coach appeared to ignore his players as he walked over to the travelling support, repeatedly raising his hands in apology. Those scenes drew immediate comparisons to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's reaction after a 4-1 defeat at Watford in November 2021, which preceded his sacking 24 hours later.

item.title: Bernardo Silva celebrates first Real Madrid goal and warns about El Clasico stakes: ‘I’m still working hard’
item.description: Bernardo Silva celebrates first Real Madrid goal and warns about El Clasico stakes: ‘I’m still working hard’ Bernardo Silva has highlighted the tactical balance Real Madrid must strike between controlling possession and maintaining their attacking threat after their 4-1 Champions League victory over RB Leipzig on matchday three. The Portuguese midfielder also celebrated scoring his first goal in the shirt and stressed the importance of the upcoming El Clasico against Barcelona. Bernardo Silva explains Real Madrid’s challenge Real Madrid’s individual quality gives them plenty of options in one-on-one situations, but Bernardo believes turning that attacking talent into a consistent team performance requires careful preparation. Speaking to Movistar Plus+ (h/t Mundo Deportivo ) after the win over Leipzig, he admitted that finding the right approach is not straightforward. “It’s difficult to strike a balance between controlling the game and not being a boring team” He expanded on the challenge, explaining how Madrid must combine possession with forward movement rather than allowing control of the ball to come at the expense of their attacking ambition. “We’re a team with players who are very aggressive individually in one-on-one situations, who like to dribble and find space. “We need to strike a balance between keeping possession and pushing forward, being direct. “That balance between controlling the game and not being a boring team, whilst remaining intense and aggressive, is difficult and we have to be very well prepared,” he added. First goal and signs of progress encourage Bernardo The Leipzig victory carried personal significance for Bernardo, who was pleased to get on the scoresheet while acknowledging that Real Madrid had to improve after a less convincing first half. He also credited Thibaut Courtois for making important interventions before the team raised its level after the break. “I’m very happy to have won this match and scored my first goal in this shirt. It was a difficult match; we were much better in the second half than in the first. “In the first half, we let them get into our box quite a few times and Thibaut was crucial,” said the Portuguese player. Bernardo believes the squad is progressing, although he warned that the early-season results must translate into sustained form if Madrid are to compete for major honours later in the campaign. “It’s good to feel that the team remains confident and is improving. I think we’re improving quite a lot; it’s only the start of the season. “We need to keep winning game by game so that, in the last three or four months, we can be in the running for trophies – which is what this club demands of you,” he noted. The midfielder also made clear that his role is secondary to the team’s needs, regardless of whether he starts or comes off the bench. Bernardo Silva scored his first goal for Real Madrid. (Picture credit: Real Madrid website) “I’m still working hard. I’m ready to help this club for one, five, ten or ninety minutes. On the day the manager feels he needs me, I’ll be ready.” Furthermore, he underlined the importance of having contributors throughout the squad rather than relying on a small group of regular starters. “For a team to function, you need more than just two or three players; you need players who feel they can make a difference. “We’ve got that with those who are playing more or less regularly; the spirit is good and we’re continuing to work hard – we’re on the right track.” Real Madrid’s El Clasico challenge carries early significance Bernardo’s focus has already shifted towards Barcelona, with the midfielder recognising that the result could have an immediate effect on the La Liga standings. Although the season remains in its early stages, he believes the points at stake make the meeting especially important. “It’s an important match; let’s not kid ourselves. We could end up three points behind, nine points behind, or even six. “We have to go into it really keen to do well, because it’s early in the season, but these are important points for us,” he concluded.

item.title: NTEL targets cheaper roaming, wider broadband access with WakaGo, AirFibre
item.description: By Juliet Umeh NATCOM Development and Investment Limited, trading as NTEL, has said its WakaGo global eSIM and AirFibre wireless broadband services will help Nigerian travellers reduce roaming costs and expand internet access for businesses and underserved communities. The company said it was leveraging the two products, alongside infrastructure sharing and existing telecommunications assets, to rebuild its network and improve connectivity across Nigeria. Speaking in an interview with Vanguard, NTEL’s Chief Technology Officer, Kingsley Uwazie, said WakaGo was designed to keep Nigerians connected while travelling abroad without purchasing local SIM cards at their destinations. “WakaGo is a global eSIM service designed to help Nigerians travelling abroad stay connected without having to buy a local SIM card at their destination or remove their existing SIM card. “The service enables users with compatible devices to access mobile data for internet services, including WhatsApp calls and messaging, while retaining their primary SIM cards for regular calls. “WakaGo operates on a pay-as-you-go basis, allowing customers to pay for their usage without being locked into a particular country or fixed bundle. “It allows Nigerians to stay connected to their loved ones locally. And the rates are very fair when you compare WakaGo to our competitors out there. “When I say fair, I mean fair against roaming charges, better than the existing roaming charges,” he explained. Uwazie cited customer experiences in Japan, the United States and China as evidence of the service’s potential, including a traveller who used WakaGo to make a video call from a crowded stadium in New York. On AirFibre, he said the wireless broadband service was designed to address the high cost of extending fibre-optic connections to homes and offices, as well as disruptions caused by frequent fibre cuts. “One of the biggest challenges we have is last-mile connection in Nigeria. There is sufficient fibre to the tower, but then last mile, fibre to the home, fibre to the office, you have problems there,” he said. He explained that AirFibre would enable internet service providers, ISPs, to use NTEL’s wireless infrastructure to reach customers without undertaking expensive fibre deployments. “We believe with wireless broadband, with sufficient wireless broadband that can provide fibre-like speeds, we can bridge that gap, and that’s where AirFibre comes in,” he said. According to him, the technology can deliver speeds of up to 1.2 gigabits per second per link, while NTEL’s network points of presence can carry more than 12 gigabits per second in capacity. “Today, AirFibre exists in Lagos and Abuja, but this is what we call our trial phase,” Uwazie said, adding that the company planned to extend the service to Ibadan, Abia State and Benin before expanding into other cities. And the rates are very fair when you compare WakaGo to our competitors out there. “When I say fair, I mean fair against roaming charges, better than the existing roaming charges,” he explained. Uwazie cited customer experiences in Japan, the United States and China as evidence of the service’s potential, including a traveller who used WakaGo to make a video call from a crowded stadium in New York. On AirFibre, he said the wireless broadband service was designed to address the high cost of extending fibre-optic connections to homes and offices, as well as disruptions caused by frequent fibre cuts. “One of the biggest challenges we have is last-mile connection in Nigeria. There is sufficient fibre to the tower, but then last mile, fibre to the home, fibre to the office, you have problems there,” he said. He explained that AirFibre would enable internet service providers, ISPs, to use NTEL’s wireless infrastructure to reach customers without undertaking expensive fibre deployments. “We believe with wireless broadband, with sufficient wireless broadband that can provide fibre-like speeds, we can bridge that gap, and that’s where AirFibre comes in,” he said. According to him, the technology can deliver speeds of up to 1.2 gigabits per second per link, while NTEL’s network points of presence can carry more than 12 gigabits per second in capacity. “Today, AirFibre exists in Lagos and Abuja, but this is what we call our trial phase,” Uwazie said, adding that the company planned to extend the service to Ibadan, Abia State and Benin before expanding into other cities. He said NTEL would also leverage infrastructure sharing and national roaming to extend mobile coverage, while satellite services would support connectivity in rural and underserved communities. “At NTEL, we believe that no single technology can solve Nigeria’s connectivity challenges,” he said. Uwazie said the company was rebuilding its business through its BET strategy, which focuses on telecommunications infrastructure, real estate and digital services. “Our aim is to keep Nigerians connected, whether you’re abroad or you’re local. We want Nigerians to trust us, and we’re building it brick by brick,” he said. The post NTEL targets cheaper roaming, wider broadband access with WakaGo, AirFibre appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Houston Rockets' Fred VanVleet racks up assists and thumbs up from C.J. Stroud in return
item.description: Houston Rockets guard Fred Vanvleet (5) talks to guard Amen Thompson (1) and forward Jabari Smith Jr. (10) after a foul was called on Dallas Mavericks at the Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. Houston Rockets won the game 128-110. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Box scores can chart any number of things on the court. Fred Van Vleet's stat line had some good (11 assists with no turnovers) and some bad (2-for-8 shooting), but there was one number no one was able to track except the man feeling it in the pit of his stomach. "All those butterflies," he said. The Houston Rockets ' point guard made his return to the court for a game that means something for the first time in more than 17 months, being forced to watch from the sidelines that whole time after tearing his ACL while working out in September 2025 . No amount of missed shots was going to be able to change VanVleet's mood, especially after helping the Rockets dismantle the Dallas Mavericks 128-110 in Wednesday night's season opener at Toyota Center. "Ah man, I've been smiling all day," he said. "I know the preseason was a little bit of a teaser, but this stuff counts. It's more pressure, it's more nerves. I was jittery for the first time in two years." Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant (7) puts up a shot around Dallas Mavericks forward P.J. Washington (25) during the first half at the Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Those nerves weren't obvious on the court for the man entering his 11th season in the NBA. With VanVleet running the show, the Rockets, who ranked near the bottom of the league in assist-to-turnover ratio last season, looked like a free-flowing offense that is much improved from last year's team that often just got the ball to Kevin Durant or Alperen Şengün and hoped they could make something happen. The veteran point guard - who, barring the preseason, hadn't played in a game since the Rockets were eliminated by the Warriors in the 2025 playoffs - set up his teammates, allowing Durant and Jabari Smith Jr., to score 30 points apiece with Şengün chipping in 23, while the Rockets had more than twice as many assists (32) as turnovers (15). "That's who he is," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said. "He's been one of the top turnover-assist ratio guy since he's been in the league. He makes the right play and the right read and gets shots up when he doesn't have anything and takes care of the ball." In VanVleet's previous two healthy seasons in Houston, he was running an offense that counted on him to provide scoring while also relying on Jalen Green's inconsistent hot streaks and a still-learning Şengün. After sitting out a year, VanVleet has returned with weapons on standby, including one of the league's all-time great scorers in Durant while also being able to count on the two-time All-Star Şengün, a blossoming Smith and the ultra-talented Amen Thompson. It's just one game, but Durant finally got to experience the steadiness of VanVleet first-hand and walked out of the arena only after leaving a five-star review. "It was amazing," Durant said. "Just his calming force. I'm one of those players that's just on edge a lot. I'm ready to go all the time. And he comes down, settles the game down. It's times where we need to just get settled down and keep the ball in our hands and take a good shot. So, just to have his presence out there, is just making my life much easier and I know as we continue to get more reps together, I'll get more comfortable and he'll get more comfortable as well." Durant wasn't the only one in the building who gave his approval. When VanVleet whipped a one-handed pass to Durant in the first half, he turned to Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud , who was sitting courtside, to see what he thought. "I just asked him how it looked, asked him to grade it," VanVleet said. "I didn't feel like it looked great. It was a nice pass, but I didn't get my full proper form. I saw him over there. Me and C.J. have developed a great relationship over the last few years. He's playing at an all-time level right now so I just wanted to see what he thought about my quarterback pass. He said it was good, he gave me two thumbs up. That's my guy, so I don't expect anything less. I would have been hurt if he had given me a thumbs down." Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: 'He was talking trash': Anthony Edwards says Miami Heat player got him all fired up
item.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images Anthony Edwards was the star of the show as the Minnesota Timberwolves beat the Miami Heat to kick off their NBA season with a win. The 25-year-old shooting guard scored 45 points in a phenomenal display and lit up the court from all angles. He was easily the best player on the night. One moment that has sparked debate is Edwards seemingly having a go at a player on Miami’s bench. He has now revealed what actually happened. Anthony Edwards says trash talk from a Miami Heat player fired him up Edwards can be unstoppable on a normal day, but when you try to get under his skin, it could make him even better. That’s exactly what happened at the Kaseya Center on Wednesday night, as the Wolves star broke his own record for most points in a season opener in his team’s entire history. After the game, Edwards was asked why he was so intense and yelling at somebody. He revealed that an opposing player was having a go at him from the Miami bench, which fired him up. There are suggestions that the player in question may have been Myron Gardner, but Edwards claimed that he doesn’t even know his name. He told Five Reasons Sports on X : “A player on their bench was talking trash in one of the dead-ball situations. I think it kinda crunk me up. “He was talking pretty crazy. When I started talking to him, he didn’t have too much more to say. I don’t really like that. If you’re gonna talk s***, keep talking s***. Don’t get quiet. I think that was the reason I was super intense tonight.” When asked if it was Gardner, he replied: “I don’t know his name.” Edwards further stated that he loves stuff like this as it gets him going every time. That should perhaps be a lesson to opposing players going forward – just leave him alone! item.title: 'An absolute disgrace!' - Jamie Carragher tears into Bruno Fernandes for 'awful attitude' and public spat with Michael Carrick after Man Utd Champions League horror show
item.description: Como 1907 v Manchester United - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport Jamie Carragher has launched a scathing attack on Bruno Fernandes, labelling the Manchester United captain an "absolute disgrace" following a public disagreement with manager Michael Carrick. The fallout comes after the Red Devils suffered a humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at the hands of Italian debutants Como. Heavy defeat in Italy exposes United tensions The pressure on Carrick intensified sharply after his side were dismantled at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium. Cesc Fabregas’ Champions League newcomers secured a comprehensive 4-1 victory , marking United's fifth loss in 11 matches across all competitions. Frustrations boiled over in the aftermath, with Fernandes publicly questioning the team's tactical setup after being substituted in the 67th minute. Carrick did not hold back in his response , issuing a pointed critique of his players' work rate. The immediate back-and-forth drew heavy fire from television pundits, with former Liverpool defender Carragher leading the condemnation of the United skipper on CBS Sports . Carragher blasts Fernandes as an 'absolute disgrace' The fallout began when Fernandes directly challenged the coaching staff's defensive strategy. "It was a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind," the midfielder claimed. Carrick quickly issued a thinly-veiled retort: "Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win." Carragher leapt to Carrick's defence, citing Lisandro Martinez's recent apology following similar criticism of the club's hierarchy after a defeat to Atletico Madrid. "We said Lisandro Martinez was bang out of order last week for calling out the hierarchy above him. For Bruno Fernandes to do that is a disgrace really," he stated. "He got player of the year last season. That was on the back of Michael Carrick becoming the manager. "He wouldn't have got that award without Carrick, because Carrick put him back in his rightful position and he then went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer. "But when you think of him as a footballer, he's a talent, but in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it's not right at all." The pundit then systematically dismantled the captain's defensive work rate. "And he's reacted like that because he's been brought off and he's been embarrassed tonight by the manager as he brought him off," Carragher added. "And when he talks about pressing, whether it's man to man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd. "I commentate on games watching Man United and he runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard - he's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it." Manchester City v
