Carrick quickly issued a thinly-veiled retort: "Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win." Carragher leapt to Carrick's defence, citing Lisandro Martinez's recent apology following similar criticism of the club's hierarchy after a defeat to Atletico Madrid. "We said Lisandro Martinez was bang out of order last week for calling out the hierarchy above him. For Bruno Fernandes to do that is a disgrace really," he stated. "He got player of the year last season. That was on the back of Michael Carrick becoming the manager. "He wouldn't have got that award without Carrick, because Carrick put him back in his rightful position and he then went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer. "But when you think of him as a footballer, he's a talent, but in terms of attitude and the way he goes about things, it's not right at all." The pundit then systematically dismantled the captain's defensive work rate. "And he's reacted like that because he's been brought off and he's been embarrassed tonight by the manager as he brought him off," Carragher added. "And when he talks about pressing, whether it's man to man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press because he does things for the crowd. "I commentate on games watching Man United and he runs all over the place like a kid in the schoolyard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard - he's not. He's killing the rest of the team doing it." Manchester City v RB Leipzig: Round of 16 Second Leg - UEFA Champions League Deep-rooted issues plaguing a 'rotten' club Widening his scope, Carragher highlighted a systemic problem at Old Trafford, noting that Fernandes has now outlasted a lengthy list of coaches. "Isn't it funny? How many managers has he had? So every single manager at Manchester United doesn't have an identity? How many managers are we on now for Bruno Fernandes? Five? They change the manager every season... Manchester United is rotten from top to bottom," he questioned. Despite the structural dysfunction, the former defender conceded Carrick's position is becoming untenable. "I said earlier on, it's not about the manager. It's everything about the club," the former Liverpool continued on his rivals. "And who has got the answers? We comment on it all the time, 'they might need to change the manager or do this, do that.' Are we ever right really? Because no one ever seems to get it right. "But listen, there's no doubt the manager needs to be changed now. Right now this can't go on for a club of the stature of Manchester United." However, Carragher praised Carrick's willingness to challenge his players publicly. "But I'm glad Michael Carrick come out and just said that about Bruno Fernandes, that he don't run, because they don't run, this team," he noted. "And what he did last season, no one's proclaiming Michael Carrick as one of the greatest managers in European football, but what he did was he come and helped his own football club last year when he was out of work himself. He's come in and he did amazing. "And the reason Manchester United are in the Champions League is because of Carrick - he got them in there. The reason they got another 100, 150 million pounds into the club is because he got them in. "No one thought he was going to get into the Champions League last season. So I feel for him a little bit. He loves the club, he's a legendary figure as a player, but obviously it's not working out for him as a manager and that needs to be changed. "But I'm delighted he brought [Fernandes] off, and I'm delighted that he had a little pop back there in the press because that's what they need some of those players." Crucial Premier League test awaits against Bournemouth FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED United have little time to dwell on their European humiliation as they prepare to host Bournemouth in the Premier League this Sunday. With five defeats already this term and a recent draw against Leeds, the domestic fixture takes on monumental importance. Anything less than a convincing victory at Old Trafford could force the board into making a swift managerial change.

item.title: “Going to be a disaster”: Ashley Young gives his verdict on hypothetical Antonio Conte to Manchester United move
item.description: “Going to be a disaster”: Ashley Young gives his verdict on hypothetical Antonio Conte to Manchester United move Manchester United’s season plunged to new depths yesterday as they were soundly defeated 4-1 by Como in northern Italy in the Champions League. Terrible season Michael Carrick’s side are now seven matches without a win and sit 13th in the Premier League and 20th in the Champions League table as things currently stand. They have also been eliminated from the League Cup after a 2-3 defeat to Brighton and Hove Albion, having squandered a 2-0 lead. Michael Carrick under pressure As a result, Michael Carrick’s position as manager is looking increasingly untenable. There have been numerous managers linked to the job, with big names such as Antonio Conte , Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe all currently available to take over the club. Nonetheless, former player Ashley Young has warned the Red Devils against pursuing a move for his former manager at Inter Milan. Young’s opinion Commenting on The Overlap (via The Manchester Evening News ), Young explained, “I’ve worked underneath him at Milan. He’s crazy, by the way. Like he is crazy. He’s a bit like Diego Simeone on the sidelines. Like you hear him non-stop.” Nonetheless, this was not the reason Young believes he would not be a good fit at Old Trafford. Explaining his methods in more detail, he added, “meetings were long. When I say long, I’m talking, if we lost the game, we could go in and do the meeting after the game and it stops literally everything and you could be there for three, four hours.” He continued, “I think that’s one of the reasons why he doesn’t last long at places because not just the players, he tries to test mentally, but the board as well and the owners.” Referring specifically to his former club’s case, he added, “there has been a lot of talk about Man United’s running stats. If they’re not going to run and Antonio Conte goes in there, it’s going to be a disaster.” United and Carrick will have a chance to respond on Sunday afternoon against AFC Bournemouth at Old Trafford. online polls

item.title: €60m+ bid incoming, Liverpool refuse to give up on France star
item.description: €60m+ bid incoming, Liverpool refuse to give up on France star Liverpool remain in the mix for one of Europe's in-demand players. They're refusing to give up and a bid is fully expected. There's no question that Liverpool need to work on their midfield. We imagined they would back in the summer as it felt natural to add to a group that struggled to control matches last season. Instead, the club sold Curtis Jones and didn't replace him. So Liverpool are actually down a midfielder at a time when it felt very sensible to sign a new one. The start to the season has shown that decision up for what it was: madness. The Reds typically struggle to control games, either through possession or halting counter-attacks, and it's led to them sitting on track for 55 points. Now, the club clearly know there's a problem and it's expected that they'll rectify things in 2027. A midfielder is on the way, in other words - but who? Liverpool in for Manu Kone TuttoMercatoWeb reports that Liverpool remain in the race for Manu Kone. The midfielder may leave AS Roma next year and both the Reds and Chelsea have him 'in their crosshairs'. On top of that, Roma feel a bid of over €60m is on its way. This comes after they rejected an offer of that amount from Chelsea in the summer. It's an interesting one, though. Kone is a good player but does seem quite similar to what Liverpool currently have. Our Value Adder model feels he's very close to Ryan Gravenberch in terms of style and is that really what the team needs right now? We're not so sure. Someone more adept at keeping the middle solid feels like a more sensible signing but then Liverpool are very much of the idea that signing the 'best' players is the way forward - not necessarily those with the best 'fit' in this squad. That could ultimately lead to Kone joining, or at least a bid going in. Roma are reluctant to sell but have grand transfer plans of their own and selling the midfielder for a large amount goes a long way to funding them. Maybe that helps Liverpool get this one over the line, then. They have other options, certainly, but it seems clear that Kone is prominently on their shortlist.

item.title: Warriors’ Yaxel Lendeborg ‘lost all respect’ for Luka Doncic after what he saw in opener
item.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Warriors’ Yaxel Lendeborg ‘lost all respect’ for Luka Doncic after what he saw in opener appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Warriors failed to start their season with a win as they fell prey to a 127-105 loss against the Los Angeles Lakers. However, apart from the loss, the Warriors rookie star Yaxel Lendeborg was particularly frustrated with the Lakers star Luka Doncic and had already lost all his respect for the Lakers franchise star. In the postgame press conference, Lendeborg admitted that witnessing the behavior of Doncic firsthand made him lose the respect he previously held for the star. “I had a lot of respect for him [ Luka Doncic ], but being in there firsthand, watching all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect for him,” Lendeborg said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Lakers guard’s tendency to show frustration toward officials has remained a recurring talking point throughout his NBA career. However, Lendeborg did not hesitate to openly criticize that behavior after making his regular-season debut in the league. Moreover, the Warriors rookie and the Slovenian superstar also had an on-court exchange during the game , which may have further contributed to Lendeborg’s frustration with Doncic. Nevertheless, Lendeborg quickly received support from Warriors veteran Draymond Green. Following the game, Green defended the rookie’s decision to stand up to the Lakers star. “Everybody’s gonna be like, ‘Oh, man, he should not talk shit to Luka, and I disagree with that shit 1000%. You f*** gonna talk to somebody, you talk until you can’t f*** talk no more,’” Green said. Despite the heated exchange and the Warriors’ eventual defeat, Lendeborg also made an impact defensively against Doncic. Though the Lakers superstar scored 23 points in the first half, the rookie was the only Golden State player who managed to slow him down effectively. According to ESPN’s tracking data, Doncic scored just two points on 0-of-4 shooting when Lendeborg served as his primary defender in half-court situations during the first half. However, the night ultimately ended in disappointment for Lendeborg and the Warriors. The rookie finished with 12 points on 5-of-11 shooting, along with three rebounds, two assists and one steal. Related: Warriors’ Draymond Green weighs in on Yaxel Lendeborg-Luka Doncic flare-up Related: Warriors’ Steve Kerr doesn’t hold back on Yaxel Lendeborg, Luka Doncic

You f*** gonna talk to somebody, you talk until you can’t f*** talk no more,’” Green said. Despite the heated exchange and the Warriors’ eventual defeat, Lendeborg also made an impact defensively against Doncic. Though the Lakers superstar scored 23 points in the first half, the rookie was the only Golden State player who managed to slow him down effectively. According to ESPN’s tracking data, Doncic scored just two points on 0-of-4 shooting when Lendeborg served as his primary defender in half-court situations during the first half. However, the night ultimately ended in disappointment for Lendeborg and the Warriors. The rookie finished with 12 points on 5-of-11 shooting, along with three rebounds, two assists and one steal. item.title: ‘This Is Not the W of 30 Years Ago’ — Jemele Hill, Cari Champion Publicly Call Out WNBA Trying To ‘Bully’ Journalists
item.description: Jemele Hill and Cari Champion criticize the WNBA's treatment of journalists, alleging pressure over negative coverage and calling for change. Jemele Hill and Cari Champion criticized the WNBA’s treatment of journalists, arguing that its approach to media coverage needs to change as the league grows. During a recent podcast discussion, Champion alleged that league personnel pressured journalists over critical coverage, while Hill questioned policies she believes restrict reporting. Jemele Hill and Cari Champion Criticize WNBA’s Treatment of Journalists On Tuesday’s episode of “Flagrant and Funny,” Champion and Hill discussed tensions between the league and journalists who cover it. Their concerns centered on media access and on how the WNBA and its teams respond to critical reporting. The former “SportsCenter” anchor called on the WNBA’s communications staff to change how they deal with journalists, arguing that the league can no longer operate as it did decades ago. “This is not the W of 30 years ago. This is the W of today,” Champion said. “Technology is different, personalities are different, people are moving different, and you’re gonna have to adjust. … And I hope that this new commissioner brings that mentality in as well.” Champion recalled an incident in which someone from the WNBA contacted her boss because they disapproved of how she presented a particular story angle. She cited the experience while discussing what she believes is a longstanding approach to dealing with critical coverage. “I think they’ve used that approach for a very long time, where they’ve tried to quietly bully certain journalists and/or people who cover them,” Champion said. The “Naked Sports” host also said that some journalists hesitate to publish critical stories because of the way teams respond to negative coverage. She argued that the problem extends beyond individual disagreements between reporters and team personnel. “A lot of it has to do with the fact that we have heard from critics that women can’t take the critique; they don’t like to be criticized,” Champion said. “A lot of journalists are tiptoeing around honest stories because the franchise, the front offices, don’t like to be criticized, don’t like to be talked about in this way, don’t want to hear what people are saying, the good and the bad.” Meanwhile, Hill questioned the WNBA’s media policies, describing some as “stifling to the growth of the league.” Her criticism concerned media-access policies she believes make it harder for journalists to cover a league that has attracted greater attention in recent seasons. item.title: Walker Kessler’s historic Lakers debut earns hilarious nickname from Shaq
item.description: With just under six minutes remaining on Wednesday night, Walker Kessler walked toward the Lakers bench, his jersey drenched in sweat, his left knee bloodied and bruised, his work finished. At that moment more than 18,000 fans inside Crypto.com Arena rose to their collective feet to give the new Lakers big man a standing ovation for his spectacular debut in the purple and gold. Kessler turned the paint into his personal playground in the Lakers season opener , throwing down 10 dunks, scoring 26 points on a perfect 12-for-12 shooting performance in the Lakers dominant 127-105 win over the Golden State Warriors. Not bad for a first impression. Walker Kessler slams home a dunk during the first half of the Lakers’ 127-105 win over the Warriors on Oct. 21, 2026 in Los Angeles. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill And somewhere, back at the “Inside the NBA” studios in Atlanta, Shaquille O’Neal was smiling. The Lakers legend christened Kessler with a hilarious new nickname during ESPN’s postgame coverage: “Milk Chamberlain.” Considering the company Kessler joined on Wednesday, it couldn’t have been more appropriate. The 7-foot-2 center became just the second player in Lakers franchise history to make at least 12 field goals without missing, joining Wilt Chamberlain, who scored 34 points on 14-for-14 shooting in 1969. His 10 dunks were the most by a Laker since O’Neal himself in 2003, according to ESPN, and reportedly established an NBA play-by-play era record. But the most frightening development for the rest of the Western Conference wasn’t Kessler’s historic stat line. It was how ridiculously easy the Lakers’ new Big Three made everything look. Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves spent Wednesday treating the rim like a dartboard, tossing alley-oops into Kessler’s general vicinity and watching their new center finish everything in sight. On one particularly outrageous possession, Doncic wrapped a behind-the-back pass around Draymond Green and delivered it directly into Kessler’s chest beneath the basket. Doncic might as well have put a bow on it. Shaquille O’Neal makes an appearance at New York Comic Con in the Jacob Javits Convention Center to promote his new comic, Vengeance Unchained, The Legend of Black Ceasar with Archie Comics on Oct. 8, 2026 in New York. ZUMAPRESS.com “When I was driving he stepped up. When I was doubled he played the pocket,” said Doncic, who finished with 28 points, eight rebounds and seven assists. “It was a very impressive game from him.” Kessler added nine rebounds and two blocks, giving the Lakers precisely the interior presence general manager Rob Pelinka envisioned when he surrendered two unprotected first-round picks and two pick swaps to acquire him. That price looked outrageous this summer. Wednesday, it looked like a bargain. Even Lakers coach JJ Redick acknowledged the significance of the moment. Luka Magic was on full display in tonight's action! 28 PTS 8 REB 7 AST 3 STL 5 3PM The Lakers pick up the win at home in their season opene

item.title: Red Wings-Wild Proposed Deal Depends on Larkin & Hughes
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 06: Dylan Larkin #71 of the Detroit Red Wings looks on in the second period while playing the Ottawa Senators at Little Caesars Arena on October 06, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Getty The Minnesota Wild remain Dylan Larkin’s preferred destination. But before the Detroit Red Wings can pull the trigger, one of the things that remains on the table is the future of Quinn Hughes. This topic has been discussed ad nauseam. It seems that every possible angle and perspective has been painfully dissected. However, a recent conversation between Jeff Marek and David Pagnotta on a recent edition of DFO Insider highlights one of the most crucial points in this entire discussion. “I was having a conversation…today with someone who said, if Dylan Larkin ends up going to Minnesota…don’t be surprised if that’s the moment where Quinn Hughes signs an extension with Minnesota…” Could a Dylan Larkin trade be the KEY to keeping Quinn Hughes in Minnesota? @JeffMarek and @TheFourthPeriod discuss how the two situations could be connected and what it means for the Wild. Ep. 4 of DFO Insider is available NOW! 🎧: https://t.co/TuEZH4pICZ 🍎:… pic.twitter.com/pAaU2jmC5O — Daily Faceoff (@DailyFaceoff) October 21, 2026 It seems that there’s an understanding that if the Red Wings trade Larkin to Minnesota, Hughes will automatically re-sign. The last thing Minnesota wants is to trade for Larkin, only to see Hughes bolt at the end of the season anyway. That’s why this deal depends on Larkin and Hughes agreeing to stay in Minnesota. Otherwise, it might seem like a fool’s errand on the Wild’s part to trade for Larkin. Hughes Likely Not Staying If Wild Can’t Land Larkin Another interesting angle is that Quinn Hughes wants to see the Red Wings send Dylan Larkin to Minnesota. It’s almost as if that is a condition for the former Norris Trophy winner to sign with Minnesota. Now, that’s an intriguing thought. It’s not that Hughes is twisting Bill Guerin’s arm to make the deal. But one does have to think that Hughes isn’t overly enthused about the Wild’s chances of truly competing for a Stanley Cup. And so, Minnesota’s top defenseman wants to see the organization land a high-end player to ensure that the team is committed to winning. That situation means that Hughes doesn’t necessarily want to see Larkin join the team. It would suggest that what Hughes wants to see is a push by the organization to make a serious splash. item.title: Bottas urged to quit F1 for good: 'Get on your bike and enjoy your life'
item.description: Ralf Schumacher believes Cadillac should replace Valtteri Bottas with Esteban Ocon , arguing that the Frenchman would be a better option for the American team. The former F1 driver made his position clear while discussing Cadillac's first season in the championship, although he stressed that his criticism of Bottas was strictly related to his performances on track. Bottas returned to Formula 1 with Cadillac in 2026 after spending a year without a race seat, joining fellow comeback driver Sergio Perez. Both arrived with considerable experience, but the American outfit has struggled to compete with the established teams during its debut campaign. Schumacher wants Cadillac to replace Bottas with Ocon Speaking on the Backstage Boxengasse podcast, Schumacher identified Haas driver Esteban Ocon as the man he would like to see Cadillac bring into its line-up: "I would definitely take Ocon immediately." The German was careful to distinguish his opinion of Bottas as a driver from his feelings towards him personally. He described the Finn as "totally likeable" and stressed that his comments should "please not be taken personally". Nevertheless, Schumacher believes Cadillac would be better served by making a change. "But from a purely sporting point of view," he explained, before suggesting that Bottas should "get on your bike and enjoy your life". Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures The remark also brought to mind Bottas's recent cycling trip from Malaysia to Singapore, which he documented on social media. Cycling has become a major part of the Finn's life away from Formula 1, and Schumacher's comments suggested that he might be better off concentrating on his interests outside racing. Ocon, meanwhile, is currently racing for Haas but does not have a seat confirmed for the 2027 season. The Frenchman continued competing in Formula 1 throughout 2025, unlike Bottas, who spent the year on the sidelines before returning with Cadillac. How Bottas and Perez have performed at Cadillac in 2026 Cadillac opted for experience when selecting its first Formula 1 driver pairing. Bottas arrived with ten Grand Prix victories from his time at Mercedes, while Perez brought six wins and several seasons of experience alongside Max Verstappen at Red Bull. However, neither driver has managed to score a point for the team so far in 2026. Cadillac has spent much of its debut campaign towards the back of the field, with both drivers regularly fighting outside the top ten. Bottas recorded one of the team's strongest results with 13th place at the Chinese Grand Prix, although his season has also been disrupted by retirements and reliability problems. Perez has similarly struggled to break into the points. item.title: The Hoddle of Coffee: Tottenham Hotspur News and Links for Thursday, October 22
item.description: Mateus Fernandes of Tottenham Hotspur warms up before the Premier League match between Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford in Manchester, United Kingdom, on October 10, 2026. (Photo by Mark Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Good morning! In recent weeks we’ve discussed new species of cats and penguins. Today it’s a plant. But this one is football related. It appears scientists have discovered a new species of plant in the Peruvian Andes. This has some blue flowers, and those who discovered it wanted to name it “salvia messii” after Lionel Messi, who plays alongside Marcos Senesi for the Argentinian national football team. A newly discovered plant in Peru has been named after Lionel Messi, called Salvia messi. The plant appears to have the same colors as Argentina 🇦🇷 pic.twitter.com/dKXswnJL8a — ESPN FC (@ESPNFC) October 17, 2026 For those keeping track, this is the sixth plant named after Lionel Messi. This leads me to ask why not one plant has been named after fitzie, particularly considering when fitzie has made famous an orchid purchased at a Virginia-based Ikea store in 2022. But that’s not the point. The world has discovered a new plant. That’s terrific. Let us discover many more. Fitzie’s track of the day: Eskimo Blue Day, by Jefferson Airplane And now for your links: Your hoddler-in-chief is currently travelling. The commentariat is entrusted to provide its own links.

item.title: NFL sends blunt message to Mike Vrabel with hefty fine over officials incident
item.description: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel has reportedly been fined $250,000 by the NFL for his conduct towards officials, with two other head coaches receiving the same punishment. According to Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer, Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni and New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn have also been hit with the hefty penalties. The fines follow growing scrutiny of interactions between coaches and officials, with the league seemingly determined to make its expectations clear. Mike Vrabel’s $250,000 fine could be overturned with good behaviour Breer described the punishments as a clear statement from the NFL but suggested there could be a way for the three coaches to avoid paying. He wrote: “That, of course, is a pretty stiff penalty and a clear statement. I’ve also heard that the fines are in abeyance, meaning they’d be on hold, and could be repealed with good behavior.” Vrabel’s fine stems from a confrontation with an official during Week 4. The Patriots coach addressed the incident after the game and insisted his comments were not derogatory. “I told him it was a terrible — I’m not going to say effing — call. I’ve said that 87 times since I’ve been a head coach. It was nothing derogatory. You’d have to ask him,” Vrabel said. “I think he was a little sensitive.” The size of the reported fine has raised eyebrows, particularly because the NFL has not publicly detailed the specific behaviour that prompted the punishment. Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio described the penalties as “borderline cartoonish”, arguing that the league had not clearly explained what the coaches had done to warrant such significant fines. There is also uncertainty surrounding what the NFL would consider good behaviour and whether the three coaches can successfully appeal. For New England, the figure is particularly striking given that the franchise received a $250,000 fine during the Spygate scandal, alongside the forfeiture of a first-round draft pick. Vrabel must now turn his attention to the Patriots’ next challenge, with the team preparing to visit the Chicago Bears on Thursday Night Football. The reported punishment also sends a warning to other head coaches, although clearer guidance from the NFL may be needed if the league expects them to avoid similar sanctions. Mike Vrabel’s $250,000 fine could be overturned with good behaviour Breer described the punishments as a clear statement from the NFL but suggested there could be a way for the three coaches to avoid paying. He wrote: “That, of course, is a pretty stiff penalty and a clear statement. I’ve also heard that the fines are in abeyance, meaning they’d be on hold, and could be repealed with good behavior.” Vrabel’s fine stems from a confrontation with an official during Week 4. The Patriots coach addressed the incident after the game and insisted his comments were not derogatory. “I told him it was a terrible — I’m not going to say effing — call. I’ve said that 87 times since I’ve been a head coach. It was nothing derogatory. You’d have to ask him,” Vrabel said. “I think he was a little sensitive.” The size of the reported fine has raised eyebrows, particularly because the NFL has not publicly detailed the specific behaviour that prompted the punishment. Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio described the penalties as “borderline cartoonish”, arguing that the league had not clearly explained what the coaches had done to warrant such significant fines. There is also uncertainty surrounding what the NFL would consider good behaviour and whether the three coaches can successfully appeal. For New England, the figure is particularly striking given that the franchise received a $250,000 fine during the Spygate scandal, alongside the forfeiture of a first-round draft pick. Vrabel must now turn his attention to the Patriots’ next challenge, with the team preparing to visit the Chicago Bears on Thursday Night Football. The reported punishment also sends a warning to other head coaches, although clearer guidance from the NFL may be needed if the league expects them to avoid similar sanctions. item.title: Clippers dethrone the Sacramento Kings in regular-season opener
item.description: Los Angeles Clippers guard Darius Garland (10) makes a deep three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. LOS ANGELES - The Los Angeles Clippers entered tonight’s regular-season opener with a lot of questions to be answered amid all the off-season turmoil and an injury list that piled on throughout the offseason. Yet, the Clippers answered the call tonight with a resounding 121-96 victory over the Sacramento Kings inside the raucous Intuit Dome crowd. Similar to their first meeting last season on Dec. 30, where the Clippers had their largest home margin of victory ever against the Kings, 131-90, the Clippers took command for nearly the entirety of the second half. Facing a Kings defense that held opponents to only a low mark of 98 points twice last season, the Clippers hit their stride from deep through the early stages, something Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue felt his team could accomplish. “We shot 52% from the field and 40% from three, those are some good numbers,” said Lue. “We just got to make sure we play the right way every possession, we have no margin for error.” Los Angeles Clippers guard Kris Dunn (8) makes a three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Nico Alba - The Sporting Tribune Los Angeles Clippers guard Kris Dunn (8) makes a three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. item.content:encoded: Los Angeles Clippers guard Darius Garland (10) makes a deep three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. LOS ANGELES - The Los Angeles Clippers entered tonight’s regular-season opener with a lot of questions to be answered amid all the off-season turmoil and an injury list that piled on throughout the offseason. Yet, the Clippers answered the call tonight with a resounding 121-96 victory over the Sacramento Kings inside the raucous Intuit Dome crowd. Similar to their first meeting last season on Dec. 30, where the Clippers had their largest home margin of victory ever against the Kings, 131-90, the Clippers took command for nearly the entirety of the second half. Facing a Kings defense that held opponents to only a low mark of 98 points twice last season, the Clippers hit their stride from deep through the early stages, something Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue felt his team could accomplish. “We shot 52% from the field and 40% from three, those are some good numbers,” said Lue. “We just got to make sure we play the right way every possession, we have no margin for error.” Los Angeles Clippers guard Kris Dunn (8) makes a three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Nico Alba - The Sporting Tribune Los Angeles Clippers guard Kris Dunn (8) makes a three pointer during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Efficiency was not a factor for the Clippers coming into this season, as they ranked third in the league last year at a near 49% shooting clip from the floor and had a near 41% mark from beyond the arc in all games against the Kings last season. Rather, it was their volume of shots that ranked amongst the bottom 10 teams in the league, coming in second-to-last with 40.5 field goals made. There was no shortage of offense tonight as the Clippers rained down 41 points in the first quarter alone, much higher than their 17-point effort last time these two faced off in Sacramento back on Feb. 6. With already seven triples deposited by the start of the second quarter, the Clippers stretched their lead to 18 points and were clicking on both ends. However, the low point of the game ensued for the Clippers following an early Kings timeout, as they roared back with a 25-14 run to close out the half while the Clippers held on to a slim 61-54 lead after missing 13 of their 18 shots during that stretch. The Clippers played a much better brand of basketball in the second half, as they spaced the floor and created opportunities for their top threats. In a game that would potentially feature the No. 5 overall pick and Clippers’ rookie sensation Keaton Wagler, it was the veterans who provided that spark. Guard Darius Garland led all scorers with 30 points on 11-for-19 shooting. In arguably his first ever season as the leader and overall officiator, Garland led the charge and has racked up double figures in all 20 games as a Clipper. “Darius I thought coming out (set) the tone early, scoring the ball offensively,” said Lue. “Then in the second half getting everyone else involved, he did a really good job of orchestrating that second half.” In a new role as the backup Center, Brook Lopez controlled the low post and paint, recording a double-double with 17 points and 11 rebounds to begin his 18th season. Los Angeles Clippers center Brook Lopez (11) makes the turnaround mid range jumper during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Nico Alba - The Sporting Tribune Los Angeles Clippers center Brook Lopez (11) makes the turnaround mid range jumper during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Wednesday October 21st, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. That back-court and front-court tandem helped ignite a massive run in the third quarter following a early Clippers timeout where the Kings trimmed it down to five. Nailing 8 of their next 13 shots in the quarter, the Clippers built their lead back up to 18 and then some, limiting the Kings to just 14 points the remaining of the quarter. The Kings were never able to trim it back into single digits the rest of the way after they were a down by a mere two-possessions. “As the second half started, I thought we did a better job of just moving the basketball, moving bodies, and making the right plays,” said Lue. “We’ve got to continue doing that every single night.” The Kings also saw contributions from their veteran stars in guard Zach LaVine and center Domantas Sabonis. Lavine dropped 28 points on 10-of-19 shooting from the floor, while the double-double machine in Sabonis put up another by the half, finishing with 14 points and 18 rebounds. Those 18 boards for Sabonis not only matched a season high from an injury-riddled year last season where he played in just 19 games, but it was also the most in a season opener for any player in Kings history. The biggest story of the night for the Kings was the royal-less debut from their No. 7 draft pick and point guard Darius Acuff Jr. While he got some good looks from the floor and attacked the rim, he shot a poor 5-for-24 from the floor and 0-for-7 from deep, finishing with 12 points. Wagler, on the other hand, got more reps in the second half with an already sizable lead. Wagler finished with 15 points and had 10 in the second half. He also collected five rebounds and five assists. In this bout of banged-up squads, the Clippers earned their 113th victory against the Kings and their 69th against them at home. With already the third best overall record in the league since the 2011-2012 season and the longest active winning-season streak of 15, the Clippers begin this 2026-27 campaign victorious. They will now take a short trip up north on Interstate 110 and take on their cross-city rivals the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday with new goals in mind. “I loved our activity, I loved our physicality,” said Lue. “We got to use our speed, we gotta be aggressive when teams attack the paint, we got to just scrap every single night (and) have each other’s backs.” Tip-off is set for 7:00 p.m.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard sounds off on Raptors’ historic season opener
item.description: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images Kawhi Leonard sounds off on Raptors’ historic season opener appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kawhi Leonard is eager to move on from his controversial stint with the Los Angeles Clippers in his return to the Toronto Raptors . He is off to a good start. Leonard helped the Raptors blow out the Chicago Bulls, 135-92, at Scotiabank Arena on Wednesday. He had 23 points, six rebounds, and four steals in 24 minutes. Their 43-point victory was the biggest season-opening win in team history. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Leonard touted their impressive performance on both ends, including leading by as much as 48 points. “You couldn’t ask for a better welcome-back game, you know. We won, we have a good team effort out there defensively, and got out on transition offensively,” said the two-time Finals MVP in the postgame interview. He acknowledged that he is still adjusting in his return to Toronto , which he led to its first title in 2019, but issued a strong message to the home crowd. “Just still getting acquainted with all my teammates, the offense, the defensive schemes. It’s the first game, so we gonna keep building and try and get better,” added Leonard. “Just thank everybody for coming out. We’re gonna try to make a special season. Hopefully, we can keep this rolling, and the best is yet to come.” Kawhi Leonard in his first postgame interview in his 2nd stint with the Toronto Raptors: “Just thank everybody for coming out. We’re gonna try to make a special season, hopefully.” “Hopefully we could keep this rolling, and the best is yet to come.” 🎥: Sportsnet 🎤:… pic.twitter.com/dknX480ONt — Omer Osman (@OmerOsman200) October 22, 2026 Immanuel Quickley had 23 points, four rebounds, seven assists, and two steals, while Scottie Barnes added 23 points, four rebounds, and three assists. The Raptors shot 45% from the field and scored 35 points off the Bulls’ 27 turnovers. The Clippers shipped Leonard to the Raptors in exchange for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, and five draft picks. Toronto will visit the Washington Wizards on Friday. Related: Raptors’ Kawhi Leonard shares clear message to those waiting for his peak form Related: Former Raptors star Serge Ibaka sends heartfelt message on Kawhi Leonard’s Toronto return

item.title: Maple Leafs Need to Have a Serious Talk about Easton Cowan
item.description: The Toronto Maple Leafs need to seriously talk about Easton Cowan's place on the team, given the start to his season. Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs cannot ignore the fact that Easton Cowan has become more than just a top prospect. The Cowboy’s start to this season has fully entrenched him as a member of the team’s top six. And that situation should lead to a serious conversation about Cowan’s place in the lineup. At the moment, Cowan has a firm grasp on a top-six lineup spot with John Tavares out with an injury. But when Tavares returns, the team needs to keep Cowan in the top six. There’s really no question about it. Cowan has looked increasingly confident playing on a line with Nick Paul and Kirill Marchenko. If anything, his goal against Columbus on Tuesday night exemplified just how far Cowan has come. EASTON COWAN WITH THE SHORTY!!! 🤠 pic.twitter.com/CGgKr9067p — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 21, 2026 With the Maple Leafs up 3-1 midway through the second period, Easton Cowan was on the penalty kill with William Nylander. The duo set off on a rush, leading to Cowan’s first career shorthanded goal. That goal exemplified two things about Cowan this season. The first thing is that the organization wants to find more playing time for the 21-year-old. And the only real place where the team could find more ice time in on the penalty kill. Cowan rewarded the Maple Leafs’ belief in him by netting the shortie. The other thing is that Easton Cowan has earned the coaching staff’s trust. He’s no longer the type of player that only goes out there in a sheltered role. He’s become the sort of player that coaches can deploy in any situation. And, at the end of the day, that makes him highly valuable to the organization. Easton Cowan Is No Longer Part of Trade Talk One of the rumors that’s out there is the fact that Cowan is no longer part of trade discussions . Two seasons ago, the Maple Leafs dangled both Cowan and Fraser Minten in front of the Carolina Hurricanes in a potential Mikko Rantanen trade. The Hurricanes had reportedly accepted one of them in the potential deal, before eventually backing out. While everyone knows how well Minten has turned out with the Boston Bruins, it’s horrifying to think what would have happened if Easton Cowan, for example, had landed in Carolina. While missing out on Rantanen really stung at the time, it’s good to know that the Maple Leafs managed to hold on to one solid prospect. Maple Leafs May End up with the Steal of First-Round in 2023 Draft All told, the Maple Leafs may end up with the biggest steal of the first round in the 2023 NHL Draft. Toronto picked Easton Cowan 28 th overall, after some rather doubtful picks. It’s worth bearing in mind that this is the draft in which Connor Bedard went first overall, Leo Carlsson second, and Adam Fantilli third. And when looking at the trajectory of these players, Cowan isn’t far behind. No, The Cowboy isn’t on track to become captain. He isn’t likely to get the massive payday

item.title: Hornets' Offseason Acquisitions Play Key Role in Opening Night Win
item.description: The Charlotte Hornets started off the 2026-27 season with a 110-103 win over the Brooklyn Nets . The Hornets were active in the offseason, retooling their roster around Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel by adding a mix of young talent and veterans. Some of their new acquisitions played a major role in their opening night win over the Nets. Naz Reid, the centerpiece of the return from the LaMelo Ball trade, had a great performance, finishing with 20 points, 11 rebounds, and seven assists, shooting 8-for-19 from the field and 4-for-10 from three. Reid was a sixth man with the Minnesota Timberwolves , but proved he could be a valuable starter in his first game in Charlotte. Veteran guard Dennis Schroder got the start in his Hornets debut, as Coby White was out with a left calf strain. Schroder played 35 minutes, finishing with 19 points, four rebounds, and six assists while shooting 7-for-13 from the floor. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect That wasn't all for the new acquisitions, as Grayson Allen provided a spark off the bench, averaging 21 points, three rebounds, and four assists, shooting 6-for-9 from the field and 5-for-8 from behind the arc. Allen's shooting was pivotal for the Hornets, and he could be a great fit for Charles Lee's system. Royce O'Neale was also solid off the bench, with eight points, four rebounds, a steal, and a block, shooting 3-for-6 from the floor and 2-for-5 from distance. The Hornets were without Knueppel, one of their best players, but still came away with a win. Knueppel finished second in Rookie of the Year voting in the 2025-26 season, averaging 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game, shooting 47.5 percent from the field and 42.5 percent from downtown. When Knueppel returns to the lineup, Charlotte's offense could reach the next level. Miller was the leader for the Hornets in shot attempts, as he had 18 points, shooting 7-for-21 from the floor and 3-for-14 from three. It wasn't an efficient game from Miller, but he should have a great 2026-27 season after signing a five-year, $209 million extension with the franchise. Starting center Moussa Diabate stood out for Charlotte, as he had 17 points, eight rebounds, three assists, and five steals while shooting 7-for-11 from the field. item.content:encoded: The Charlotte Hornets started off the 2026-27 season with a 110-103 win over the Brooklyn Nets . The Hornets were active in the offseason, retooling their roster around Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel by adding a mix of young talent and veterans. Some of their new acquisitions played a major role in their opening night win over the Nets. Naz Reid, the centerpiece of the return from the LaMelo Ball trade, had a great performance, finishing with 20 points, 11 rebounds, and seven assists, shooting 8-for-19 from the field and 4-for-10 from three. Reid was a sixth man with the Minnesota Timberwolves , but proved he could be a valuable starter in his first game in Charlotte. Veteran guard Dennis Schroder got the start in his Hornets debut, as Coby White was out with a left calf strain. Schroder played 35 minutes, finishing with 19 points, four rebounds, and six assists while shooting 7-for-13 from the floor. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect That wasn't all for the new acquisitions, as Grayson Allen provided a spark off the bench, averaging 21 points, three rebounds, and four assists, shooting 6-for-9 from the field and 5-for-8 from behind the arc. Allen's shooting was pivotal for the Hornets, and he could be a great fit for Charles Lee's system. Royce O'Neale was also solid off the bench, with eight points, four rebounds, a steal, and a block, shooting 3-for-6 from the floor and 2-for-5 from distance. The Hornets were without Knueppel, one of their best players, but still came away with a win. Knueppel finished second in Rookie of the Year voting in the 2025-26 season, averaging 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game, shooting 47.5 percent from the field and 42.5 percent from downtown. When Knueppel returns to the lineup, Charlotte's offense could reach the next level. Miller was the leader for the Hornets in shot attempts, as he had 18 points, shooting 7-for-21 from the floor and 3-for-14 from three. It wasn't an efficient game from Miller, but he should have a great 2026-27 season after signing a five-year, $209 million extension with the franchise. Starting center Moussa Diabate stood out for Charlotte, as he had 17 points, eight rebounds, three assists, and five steals while shooting 7-for-11 from the field. It's a strong start to the season for the Hornets, as they look to make it into the playoffs for the first time since the 2015-16 season.

item.title: Florentino Perez to miss Barcelona vs Real Madrid El Clasico at Spotify Camp Nou
item.description: Florentino Perez to miss Barcelona vs Real Madrid El Clasico at Spotify Camp Nou Real Madrid president Florentino Perez will not attend Sunday’s El Clasico against Barcelona at Spotify Camp Nou, according to Mundo Deportivo , with the decision also ruling out the traditional pre-match lunch between the clubs’ directors. His absence comes amid strained institutional relations between the Spanish giants, ensuring there will be no meeting with Barcelona president Joan Laporta before kick-off. The fixture is already attracting attention for Jose Mourinho’s return to Barcelona, but the lack of a presidential reunion adds more controversy to a rivalry that has increasingly extended beyond the pitch. Florentino Perez absence means no directors’ lunch Perez will not travel to Barcelona for the latest meeting between the clubs, continuing a pattern of absences from Camp Nou in recent seasons. According to the report, the usual gathering between the two boards will not take place either, removing a long-standing part of the pre-match protocol surrounding El Clasico. Florentino Perez will not attend this season’s El Clasico at Camp Nou. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The relationship between Barcelona and Real Madrid has deteriorated since Real Madrid began pursuing the Negreira case publicly. The dispute has contributed to a breakdown in institutional relations, making the absence of both Perez and the traditional directors’ luncheon more than a routine scheduling detail. Real Madrid will still have a presence in the VIP area, although the representation is expected to be more limited than in previous editions. At last season’s corresponding Clasico at Camp Nou, Pirri, Real Madrid’s honorary president, was the only representative from the Madrid club in the VIP box. This time, a Real Madrid vice-president is expected to attend. Tyler, the Creator among expected El Clasico guests Barcelona no longer have any relationship with Real Madrid. (Photo by JAVIER SORIANO/AFP via Getty Images) Attention will also extend beyond the club executives, with the list of VIPs and dignitaries still awaiting final confirmation. Tyler, The Creator is expected to be among those attending. The artist’s logo, alongside his GOLF brand, will feature on the front of Barcelona’s shirt for the occasion. His anticipated presence offers a different kind of spotlight for the fixture, which combines sporting rivalry, commercial visibility and institutional tension. Yet the most consequential absence may be Perez’s.

item.title: “Help the team as best I can”
item.description: “Help the team as best I can” Raphael Onyedika talks about his first home win as an Eagle, previous experience of Dortmund and his physical stamina. Raphael, congratulations on the first home win. How did it feel to stand in front of the fans with three points for the first time? “Thanks! There were great emotions. Regardless of the feelings it triggered in me, it was first and foremost important to have picked up three points against Köln – for us as a team just as much as for the fans.” You’re the only player who’s completed 690 of a possible 690 competitive minutes this season. Where does that endurance come from? “I’m in top shape and want to help the team as best I can. The team’s success is the priority. The more I can contribute to that, the better. In general, we all do a lot of training on the physical aspect because that’s the basis for how we play. It certainly helps me that I’ve been used to playing two matches a week in the last four or five years.” Who is your idol? “Ronaldinho was one of my heroes when I was younger. In terms of playing style, I try to take some things from Paul Pogba in his best years. But he also had a slightly different profile as a midfielder to me.” You’ve mostly played alongside Mario Götze and Noel Aseko so far. Does your game change depending on which of them is next to you, or do all the tasks remain the same? “The guys next to me are different players in some ways, but that doesn’t change anything for me. I’m the most defensive of our midfielders. In any case, the coach wants us to develop a connection with every single teammate. I take that on board and enjoy playing with Mario, Noel or also Oscar Højlund.” You returned from international duty early. Why was that? “The idea came from the club, so that we had more time together to prepare at the end of the international period. After getting the okay from the Nigeria Football Federation, I came back early.” Do you remember your first match against Dortmund? “Very well, actually. First matchday in the Champions League two years ago with Club Brugge. We held our own really well for a long time and had chances to lead 1-0 or even 2-0. The game flipped in the final 20 minutes, BVB scored three goals in the final quarter of an hour and won 3-0. It was strange: the feeling that we held our own well and yet deserved to lose by that margin.” You go to Dortmund on Saturday, in front of around 80,000 people. Have you ever played in a comparable stadium? “I can’t recall playing in front of such a big crowd. I’ve heard a lot about the stadium, the atmosphere and not least the opposition team. I think it’s going to be nice and challenging. We are doing everything we can to be perfectly prepared, mentally as well. It’s vital to remember that there is always room for improvement, even after a win like the one against Cologne. We are a good side, but we have to make sure we get the details right over the full 90 to 95 minutes of every single game!”

item.title: Vinicius sinking, Camavinga’s rise | Three takeaways from Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig
item.description: Vinicius sinking, Camavinga’s rise | Three takeaways from Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig For the second straight game, Real Madrid racked up a 4-1 win last night against RB Leipzig, and it is safe to say that the result was thoroughly deserved. There were moments of panic in the game from which Thibaut Courtois was forced to make extra-terrestrial saves to keep his side alive. Once they took the lead, however, Real Madrid inflicted serial damage on the visitors and found themselves 3-0 up by the 83rd minute. The visitors then pulled one back, but Yan Diomande delivered the final blow with a wonderful strike. Madrid Universal brings you three takeaways from Real Madrid 4-1 RB Leipzig . Vinicius’ future looks bleak Being suspended in La Liga for four games, Vinicius Jr.’s only chance of playing football now comes in the UEFA Champions League. Jose Mourinho thus decided to hand the player a start last night, hoping he would redeem himself. Vinicius Jr. was not at his best against RB Leipzig. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) While Vinicius was slightly better than he had looked in recent games, he was again outperformed and overshadowed, even though he replaced him for only the final 20 minutes. In 70 minutes on the field, the Brazilian star failed to rack up a single key pass or accurate cross. He did have two shots on target, but neither really looked like a scoring position. What is more appalling is that the Brazilian star did not complete a single dribble in 70 minutes – something that is very unlike him and a clear indication that he is slowly but surely sinking under pressure. Coming on to replace him, meanwhile, Diomande scored a stunning goal, racked up one key pass and looked like a regular threat down the left flank for Real Madrid. The difference between him and Vinicius was clear as day. Given how matters are progressing, Vinicius appears to be slowly reconciling to the fact that he is losing his spot in the side and that there is nothing he can do about it. His decline is unfortunate and difficult to watch, but Diomande appears to be growing into a deserved starter on the left wing. Camavinga’s big statement Camavinga started alongside Bernardo Silva against RB Leipzig. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Jose Mourinho completely changed the look of Real Madrid’s midfield last night, bringing on Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into the lineup as the double pivot. Both players have not had a lot of minutes in recent weeks – particularly the Frenchman who only saw fringe minutes after the international break despite doing well for Zinedine Zidane and France. The difference between him and Vinicius was clear as day. Given how matters are progressing, Vinicius appears to be slowly reconciling to the fact that he is losing his spot in the side and that there is nothing he can do about it. His decline is unfortunate and difficult to watch, but Diomande appears to be growing into a deserved starter on the left wing. Camavinga’s big statement Camavinga started alongside Bernardo Silva against RB Leipzig. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Jose Mourinho completely changed the look of Real Madrid’s midfield last night, bringing on Bernardo Silva and Eduardo Camavinga into the lineup as the double pivot. Both players have not had a lot of minutes in recent weeks – particularly the Frenchman who only saw fringe minutes after the international break despite doing well for Zinedine Zidane and France. After a long time, Camavinga played all 90 minutes for Los Blancos and he dropped a performance that once again showed the world why he was so highly rated at one point. He may not have finished with a goal or an assist, but the control he provided in midfield was far superior to what Aurelien Tchouameni usually offers. In 90 minutes, Camavinga completed 92% of his passes, 67% of long balls and completed 100% of the three dribbles he attempted. Defensively, he stood out with six recoveries, an interception, three tackles won and a staggering 14 duels won. For Camavinga to come back into such good form, needless to say, comes as massive news for Real Madrid and Jose Mourinho. Moreover, his positive partnership with Bernardo Silva hands the manager a new rotational option in midfield. Momentum when it’s needed most The wind is fresh in Real Madrid’s sails, and for the first time this season, Mourinho’s men seem to be treading a path with a clear plan and good confidence. Real Madrid now have the momentum. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) The timing of such a purple patch, in that sense, could not have been any better. Having scored eight goals and conceded just two in their last two games, Real Madrid will now believe in their chances against Barcelona at the weekend. For a long time, the Catalans were seen as overwhelming favourites against Real Madrid, especially because of Los Blancos’ midfield situation. With order now restored and some semblance of stability in the department, Real Madrid also have a good chance of capitalising on the Clasico. The importance of the momentum the team currently possesses, in that sense, cannot be understated and all eyes now shift to the weekend’s game against Barcelona which is massive for the title race. A win, and Real Madrid are back within three points and well within reach of the lead in La Liga. A defeat, however, will put them nine points behind Barcelona and in a position of great weakness in the domestic competition.

item.title: Chargers in trouble over Travis Kelce incident as major NFL punishment looms
item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley could face a significant NFL fine after his controversial tackle on Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce during their 22-6 defeat. The incident has attracted attention after Kelce appeared to tweak his ankle during the play. The veteran tight end briefly left the game before returning, easing concerns among Chiefs supporters. However, the tackle has continued to generate debate, with questions being raised over whether Henley used an illegal hip-drop technique. Daiyan Henley could face NFL fine for Travis Kelce tackle Clips of the tackle have circulated online, with Chiefs fans and analysts questioning the legality of Henley’s challenge. The NFL prohibits hip-drop tackles because of the injury risk involved. The banned technique involves a defender unweighting their body, swivelling their hips and dropping onto a ball carrier’s legs to bring them down. The play involving Kelce has prompted scrutiny over whether Henley’s tackle met those criteria. However, the league has not officially confirmed that it is investigating the incident or announced any disciplinary action. If the NFL determines that Henley committed an illegal hip-drop tackle, he could face a five-figure penalty. According to the league’s official website, the baseline fine for a first offence is $17,911, rising to $23,882 for repeat violations. Those figures mean the Chargers linebacker could face a costly consequence if the league rules against him. However, any potential punishment remains unconfirmed. Kelce’s brief absence from the game also raised concerns for Kansas City, given his importance to the Chiefs’ offence. He was able to return, while head coach Andy Reid offered a reassuring update after the victory. Reid indicated that Kelce might be sore but said he would “be ok”. The Chiefs will now hope their tight end avoids any lingering problems as they continue their unbeaten start to the season. Meanwhile, the Chargers remain winless after six games, adding to the pressure following another defeat. Henley’s situation will depend on the NFL’s review and whether the league determines that the tackle breached its rules. Until an official decision is announced, a fine remains a possibility rather than a confirmed punishment. item.title: JD Vance Meets His Favorite NFL Team, but Most Players Walk Past
item.description: Photo by Kenny Holston-Pool/Getty Images Vice President JD Vance visited his favorite NFL team, but the players’ reaction wasn’t what he expected. A new video captured the awkward moment Bengals players walked right past the VP after practice. How Cincinnati Bengals players interacted with the vice president Cincinnati Bengals players gave Vice President JD Vance a notably cold reception during his surprise visit to Paycor Stadium, according to NBC 5 Cincinnati. The Ohio native stopped by after speaking at a rally in the Cincinnati suburb of Sharonville on Wednesday. Most players offered little more than a passing nod as they walked past him toward the locker room after practice. JD Vance greets Bengals players on the way out pic.twitter.com/lMKvYRpMfE — Charlie Clifford (@char_cliff) October 21, 2026 Sports Director Charlie Clifford’s 18-second video captured tight end Drew Sample fist-bumping Vance’s son Vivek before briefly shaking the vice president’s hand. Sample appeared to be the only player in the clip who shook Vance’s hand. Clifford later explained on air that Vance was spending time with the players as practice ended. Head coach Zac Taylor did shake Vance’s hand before heading into the locker room. A separate video from Cincinnati Enquirer reporter Kelsey Conway captured that interaction. Star quarterback Joe Burrow told reporters he did not get a chance to meet with Vance. “He, uhh, came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice, so I didn’t get to,” Burrow said. The 29-year-old added he only learned about the visit after practice had already started. Burrow deflected a question about his reaction to the visit by turning the focus to himself. “A lot of people around. You know, that’s what I love about what I do is, it brings a lot of people together, and people want to take time out of their day to come and watch what we do, watch what I do, and watch all the work that I’ve put in, to come and watch greatness,” Burrow said. Vance grew up in Middletown, roughly a 45-minute drive from downtown Cincinnati. The 3-2 Bengals will face the 4-2 Ravens in Baltimore on Sunday. The post JD Vance Meets His Favorite NFL Team, but Most Players Walk Past appeared first on Reality Tea .

item.title: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg ‘lost all respect’ for Luka Doncic
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Matched up with Luka Doncic, Yaxel Lendeborg, the Warriors’ bold and brash rookie, came away with at least one lesson from his NBA debut. “Being in there firsthand, just watching all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect, man,” Lendeborg said after Golden State’s 127-105 season-opening loss to the Lakers . “That was awful.” The most entertaining part of a blowout loss for the Warriors was undoubtedly Lendeborg’s ongoing back-and-forth with the Lakers’ equally loud-mouthed superstar . Lendeborg finished with 12 points, four personal fouls and one technical in 29 minutes. Yaxel Lendeborg defends Luka Doncic during the Warriors’ 127-105 loss to the Lakers on Oct. 21, 2026 in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images He often drew the defensive matchup with Doncic, who went off for a game-high 28 with nine free throws. But Lendeborg’s biggest takeaway was all Doncic’s extracurriculars that came after the whistle. “Like, me getting frustrated, it’s not about the foul getting called. It’s about him complaining the entire game,” Lendeborg said. “Then you get the foul called — congratulations, bro — and you talk to me like you did something great? That’s just weak. It kind of threw me off for a while. Because like I said, I had so much respect for him. Gone, man.” Though Doncic only made it to the line nine times, Lendeborg said it felt like 30. Doncic mostly only ran his mouth on the court, merely saying afterward that the No. 11 overall pick was “talking like crazy.” Lendeborg, on the other hand, was happy to get into the nitty gritty. “I said a couple cuss words,” Lendeborg said. “That’s why I got the technical. But I was letting him know, because he was laughing and talking all this because of one foul call.” Lendeborg bit on one of Doncic’s pump fakes midway through the first half, and the two were off and running — their mouths, anyway. Doncic pointed and laughed. Lendeborg responded. At one point, Lendeborg started putting both his hands behind his back when guarding Doncic. Yaxel Lendeborg (left) and Luka Doncic look on during a break in the action in the Warriors’ loss to the Lakers. NBAE via Getty Images “I tried my best,” he said. “I still got called.” The back-and-forth continued for the remainder of the first half, hitting an inflection point after Lendeborg successfully defended Doncic on a step-back 3. He followed him back down the court, yapping all the way, until he was T’d up for the first time in his career. Doncic returned the favor after banking in a half-court shot at the buzzer going into halftime. item.content:encoded: LOS ANGELES — Matched up with Luka Doncic, Yaxel Lendeborg, the Warriors’ bold and brash rookie, came away with at least one lesson from his NBA debut. “Being in there firsthand, just watching all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect, man,” Lendeborg said after Golden State’s 127-105 season-opening loss to the Lakers . “That was awful.” The most entertaining part of a blowout loss for the Warriors was undoubtedly Lendeborg’s ongoing back-and-forth with the Lakers’ equally loud-mouthed superstar . Lendeborg finished with 12 points, four personal fouls and one technical in 29 minutes. Yaxel Lendeborg defends Luka Doncic during the Warriors’ 127-105 loss to the Lakers on Oct. 21, 2026 in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images He often drew the defensive matchup with Doncic, who went off for a game-high 28 with nine free throws. But Lendeborg’s biggest takeaway was all Doncic’s extracurriculars that came after the whistle. “Like, me getting frustrated, it’s not about the foul getting called. It’s about him complaining the entire game,” Lendeborg said. “Then you get the foul called — congratulations, bro — and you talk to me like you did something great? That’s just weak. It kind of threw me off for a while. Because like I said, I had so much respect for him. Gone, man.” Though Doncic only made it to the line nine times, Lendeborg said it felt like 30. Doncic mostly only ran his mouth on the court, merely saying afterward that the No. 11 overall pick was “talking like crazy.” Lendeborg, on the other hand, was happy to get into the nitty gritty. “I said a couple cuss words,” Lendeborg said. “That’s why I got the technical. But I was letting him know, because he was laughing and talking all this because of one foul call.” Lendeborg bit on one of Doncic’s pump fakes midway through the first half, and the two were off and running — their mouths, anyway. Doncic pointed and laughed. Lendeborg responded. At one point, Lendeborg started putting both his hands behind his back when guarding Doncic. Yaxel Lendeborg (left) and Luka Doncic look on during a break in the action in the Warriors’ loss to the Lakers. NBAE via Getty Images “I tried my best,” he said. “I still got called.” The back-and-forth continued for the remainder of the first half, hitting an inflection point after Lendeborg successfully defended Doncic on a step-back 3. He followed him back down the court, yapping all the way, until he was T’d up for the first time in his career. Doncic returned the favor after banking in a half-court shot at the buzzer going into halftime. Coach Steve Kerr said it was “kind of ridiculous” that Lendeborg was the only one to draw a technical in the exchange. But he didn’t have a problem with his rookie’s confidence. Yaxel Lendeborg looks on during the Warriors’ loss to the Lakers. NBAE via Getty Images “They were jawing at each other. I think it was the words Yaxel chose that got him the T,” Kerr said, acknowledging that Doncic “kind of lured him in.” Lendeborg looked at it differently, despite Doncic’s well-known proclivity for elevating his play when an opponent pokes the bear. The rest of the league will learn he feeds off it, too. “I feel like it works for me, for sure. On the defensive end I feel like it worked,” Lendeborg said. “I know he has a reputation for that. That’s probably why the half-court shot went in. But I didn’t really see nothing else. I definitely thought that he was gonna do more than that.” If we learned anything from Lendeborg’s NBA debut, he may be the league’s most captivating newcomer, possibly even a spiritual successor to Draymond Green. Lendeborg, however, walked away wide-eyed for another reason. “I got to see what the NBA’s like, man. A lot of flopping, a lot of foul baiting, a lot of praying to the ref,” Lendeborg said. “Interesting first game, for sure.”

item.title: Mets predicted to sign rival Phillies' $10.2M high-contact All-Star to replace Jorge Polanco
item.description: Mets predicted to sign rival Phillies' $10.2M high-contact All-Star to replace Jorge Polanco originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Phillies could have a new-look roster next season as they try to figure out how to get back to the World Series. Their season ended at the hands of the Atlanta Braves in the Wild Card round, which likely isn't how they wanted to go out. The Phillies will now turn their attention to the offseason, and it remains unclear what comes next for All-Star Alec Bohm. “Even though it was a dreadful start to the season, it was good to see Bohm bounce back as the season progressed. Overall, .249/.315/.383 with 15 home runs and 88 RBI. The numbers certainly improved for the slugger, and he should be seen as a desirable target in free agency. However, whether or not he will be back with the Phillies remains to be seen. This is a team that is trying to get a little bit younger, and handing out another potential long-term deal to a veteran might not be what they want to do,” SI’s Nick Ziegler wrote. There is considerable uncertainty surrounding Bohm's future in Philadelphia. Based on the latest speculation, it appears increasingly possible that he will not return. “It doesn’t sound like Alec Bohm is especially likely to return to the Phillies,” Bleacher Report’s Tim Kelly wrote. Bohm should have several options in free agency, as he is a consistent contact hitter. MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand believes Bohm could join the New York Mets and take over at first base. “The Mets’ production at first base (.667 OPS) was third worst in the Majors, but Jorge Polanco is signed for $20 million next season. Their .684 OPS at third base ranked 19th in the Majors, but with Bo Bichette signed for $42 million in 2027 (with another $42 million player option for ‘28), the hot corner wouldn’t appear to be available. Owner Steve Cohen could look past the money owed to Polanco if he believes Bohm is a good fit for the Mets, who are coming off of two straight seasons without reaching the postseason,” Feinsand wrote. It is safe to say that the Jorge Polanco experiment hasn't gone according to plan for the Mets. They could use him as a designated hitter or at second base, potentially opening up another spot for Bohm. Bohm still has plenty of upside and could give New York another option in its lineup. Bohm played on a $10.2 million contract with the Phillies. The Mets could look to poach a player from one of their division rivals as they try to improve their roster. New York will be looking to have a better season, and adding Bohm could help the team accomplish that goal. item.title: Ebola Case: Keyamo Orders 21-Day No-Fly Restriction For 46 Contacts
item.description: In a measure to contain the spread of the Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) following a confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, said he has directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to place 46 persons identified as contacts of an Ebola-affected patient on a no-fly list for at least 21 days. The minister disclosed the directives in a statement posted on his verified X account following a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate. Keyamo said he has also ordered FAAN to strengthen Ebola surveillance and response protocols across all international airports, including enhanced health screening, temperature checks and travel history monitoring. According to Keyamo, the health minister provided a list of 44 persons who came into contact with an affected female patient at a hospital after she developed symptoms of Ebola, alongside two members of her domestic staff. “This evening, I held a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate over the Ebola scourge,” Keyamo stated. “He shared with me a list of 44 persons with whom the affected person came in contact at the hospital when she had developed the symptoms and an additional two persons who are her domestic staff.” He explained that aviation authorities were required to prevent the individuals from travelling by air for at least 21 days, corresponding to the period within which Ebola symptoms may develop following exposure. “Whilst efforts are ongoing to isolate them for now until there is certainty they had not been infected with the virus, the Aviation authorities are required to put them on a no-fly list for at least 21 days (which is the period that the symptoms are normally expected to manifest),” he said. Keyamo disclosed that he had directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) to immediately notify domestic and international airlines of the restriction. “I have therefore directed the NCAA to immediately inform all local and international airlines of this development,” he stated. Photo illustration of Aviation Minister, Festus Keyamo, and an airport. The minister also instructed FAAN to intensify health surveillance and Ebola response measures at international airports nationwide. According to him, the airport authority has already introduced enhanced health screening, temperature checks, travel history tracking and digital health declarations. “I have also directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to heighten Ebola response and surveillance protocols across all international airports,” he said. “Measures already being implemented by FAAN include enhanced health screenings, temperature checks, travel history tracking, digital health declarations, and strict inter-agency coordination with the NCDC following regional outbreak alerts earlier.” The minister’s statement did
