item.content:encoded: In a measure to contain the spread of the Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) following a confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, said he has directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to place 46 persons identified as contacts of an Ebola-affected patient on a no-fly list for at least 21 days. The minister disclosed the directives in a statement posted on his verified X account following a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate. Keyamo said he has also ordered FAAN to strengthen Ebola surveillance and response protocols across all international airports, including enhanced health screening, temperature checks and travel history monitoring. According to Keyamo, the health minister provided a list of 44 persons who came into contact with an affected female patient at a hospital after she developed symptoms of Ebola, alongside two members of her domestic staff. “This evening, I held a virtual meeting with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate over the Ebola scourge,” Keyamo stated. “He shared with me a list of 44 persons with whom the affected person came in contact at the hospital when she had developed the symptoms and an additional two persons who are her domestic staff.” He explained that aviation authorities were required to prevent the individuals from travelling by air for at least 21 days, corresponding to the period within which Ebola symptoms may develop following exposure. “Whilst efforts are ongoing to isolate them for now until there is certainty they had not been infected with the virus, the Aviation authorities are required to put them on a no-fly list for at least 21 days (which is the period that the symptoms are normally expected to manifest),” he said. Keyamo disclosed that he had directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) to immediately notify domestic and international airlines of the restriction. “I have therefore directed the NCAA to immediately inform all local and international airlines of this development,” he stated. Photo illustration of Aviation Minister, Festus Keyamo, and an airport. The minister also instructed FAAN to intensify health surveillance and Ebola response measures at international airports nationwide. According to him, the airport authority has already introduced enhanced health screening, temperature checks, travel history tracking and digital health declarations. “I have also directed the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to heighten Ebola response and surveillance protocols across all international airports,” he said. “Measures already being implemented by FAAN include enhanced health screenings, temperature checks, travel history tracking, digital health declarations, and strict inter-agency coordination with the NCDC following regional outbreak alerts earlier.” The minister’s statement did not identify the affected patient, disclose the location of the hospital where the contacts occurred or specify whether the infection was contracted within Nigeria. It also did not indicate that any of the 46 identified contacts had tested positive for Ebola. FAAN Heightens Vigilance Across Airports The development came after FAAN, on Wednesday, said it was maintaining heightened vigilance across airport operations. It said it is working with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), Port Health Services, Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) and other relevant agencies to support ongoing containment efforts. The agency stated that early identification of the case and commencement of contact tracing underscore the importance of established public health protocols, effective surveillance and inter-agency collaboration in responding to potential health threats. “FAAN is maintaining heightened vigilance across airport operations and will continue to coordinate with public health authorities, align its response with further guidance and support additional measures considered necessary to safeguard passengers, airport personnel and the wider public,” it said in a statement by the Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Henry Agbebire. It urged passengers, airport users, airlines and other stakeholders to remain calm, vigilant and cooperative with health officials. “The public is also advised to rely on verified information and avoid spreading unconfirmed reports,” it added. “FAAN reassures the travelling public of its continued readiness to work with relevant agencies to protect public health and support the safe operation of Nigeria’s airports.” The Federal Government confirmed a case of the virus in the FCT on Wednesday. This combo photo shows NCDC officials on duty in Nigeria, and response team members helping to wear protective suits before burying a person suspected of having died from Ebola in Bunia, in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, on May 25, 2026. (Channels TV/GLODY MURHABAZI / AFP). FG Assures Nigerians Of Containment Strategies The Presidential Task Force on Ebola Preparedness, Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats has assured Nigerians it can handle Ebola in the country. The Chairman of the Task Force and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, said this while speaking to newsmen after the group’s emergency meeting at the State House on Wednesday. Gbajabiamila said the Task Force has been working behind the scenes since it was inaugurated in June this year. He added that this is why it was easy to detect the index case discovered yesterday. “It’s very important to note this. Since the issue of Ebola came up in June, there have been about 44, 000 flights in and out of Nigeria. So, it’s because of what the Ministry of Health, the task force and all the agencies have been doing. All hands have been on deck. “The passenger with the disease showed no symptoms, which came four days after the woman got into Abuja, and it was the identification process and the protocols that were put in place that enabled the quick identification. That also speaks to the country’s capacity and ability to deal with this disease as best as we can,” he said, according to a statement by presidential spokesman Bayo Onanuga. He assured Nigerians that the Task Force would strengthen whatever needed strengthening, the protocols, and ensure more rigorous enforcement moving forward. “The Task Force is on top of it. NCDC is on top of it; everyone is on deck. We must build community trust and avoid panic, but it’s also important to state clearly that this is a collaborative effort between the government and the people. He appealed to all Nigerians to respond to calls for compliance for the good of all. Health workers in Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) simulate using a manikin the evacuation protocols of deceased victims of Ebola during a training by a medical charity in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) at Ongata Rongai, Kajiado County in Kenya on July 10, 2026. ‘Nigeria Has Competent Health Authorities’ Meanwhile, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Ali Pate, said Nigeria has competent health authorities, including private hospital operators and agencies, Immigration, Aviation, Interior, and subnational actors, who have put surveillance systems in place across the country, ready to respond. “We have been conducting contact tracing diligently and isolating those contacts of the index imported case in this country. We will continue to do that, and we want to reassure Nigerians that the federal government, alongside its technical partners, the World Health Organisation, the Africa Centre for Disease Control, and our own Nigeria Centre for Disease Control, have activated the incident management system across the various pillars. “They are working day and night diligently, and our hospital cap

item.title: Man Utd dressing room DRAMA! Michael Carrick fires back at Bruno Fernandes in public war of words after Red Devils humiliated by Como in Champions League horror show
item.description: Michael Carrick Bruno Fernandes Manchester United Como - Getty Images Manchester United’s season hit a new low on Wednesday night as a disastrous 4-1 defeat to Como sparked a public war of words between Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes. The humiliating Champions League result has left the manager’s future in serious doubt after a performance that lacked both tactical discipline and physical effort. Nightmare in northern Italy The Red Devils endured a miserable evening at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium, crashing to their fifth defeat in just 11 matches this term. Wednesday's dismal European outing also stretched their current winless streak to seven games across all competitions. The United skipper was withdrawn after 67 minutes on a night where the Premier League giants were completely outclassed. The aftermath quickly descended into chaos as captain and manager took bitter public swipes at each other over the root cause of the Italian collapse. Tactics versus effort debate Following his substitution, Fernandes pointed the finger directly at the dugout. The Portuguese playmaker questioned the game plan , stating: "It was a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind." When informed of those remarks during his post-match media duties, the 45-year-old manager refused to take the criticism lying down. Instead, Carrick fired back by openly questioning the basic work rate of his dressing room. "We actually were half-pressed man-to-man in the second half and then conceded a goal from that," Carrick explained. He then delivered a pointed message to Fernandes: "And whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win." Como 1907 v Manchester United - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 Mounting pressure and fan apologies The messy public feud heavily intensifies the spotlight on the United boss. Having earned a new two-year deal in May following a third-place league finish, this sudden domestic and continental slump has firmly jeopardised his position. After apologising directly to the travelling support at the final whistle, the head coach was pressed on whether he feared the sack. He insisted his focus remained entirely on the club's frustrated fanbase rather than his own employment status. "Listen, I've not given my own position any thought. This is for the supporters; I was one of them watching that, and I wasn't happy at all," Carrick revealed. "I'm really angry, to be honest. We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight wasn't acceptable. I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure." item.title: Standard Chartered names Adelagun CEO
item.description: By Kingsley Adegboye Standard Chartered Bank Nigeria Limited has confirmed Ayodeji Adelagun as its Chief Executive Officer following regulatory approval by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). Adelagun has served as acting CEO since January 2026. He brings more than 26 years of banking and financial markets experience across Africa to the role. Since joining Standard Chartered in 2007, he has held several senior positions, including Executive Director and Head of Markets for Nigeria and Africa, and Head of Rates and Credit Trading for West Africa. He is also Chairman of Standard Chartered Capital and Advisory Nigeria and Head of Markets, Africa. Commenting on his appointment, Adelagun said Nigeria remained a significant long-term growth market for the bank. He stated: “Nigeria represents a significant long-term opportunity for Standard Chartered, and our ambition is to build on the strength of our franchise to deliver even greater value for our clients and the wider economy. “As we enter this next chapter, my focus will be on deepening our client relationships, driving disciplined and sustainable growth, and bringing the full strength of Standard Chartered’s international network and capabilities to clients in Nigeria.” A Fellow of the Financial Markets Dealers Association (FMDA), Adelagun led the workstream that introduced benchmark bonds in Nigeria, helping deepen the domestic bond market and support the country’s inclusion in the JP Morgan Emerging Markets Index. He also pioneered bond trading desks at FSDH and Standard Chartered Bank. Earlier in his career, he worked in Banking Operations, Commercial Banking and Treasury at Access Bank Plc. The post Standard Chartered names Adelagun CEO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Padres predicted to sign Yankees' $10M high-energy Silver Slugger to pair with Fernando Tatis
item.description: Padres predicted to sign Yankees' $10M high-energy Silver Slugger to pair with Fernando Tatis originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . This is going to be a big offseason for Jazz Chisholm as he faces decisions about his future in free agency. The New York Yankees second baseman was left out of the starting lineup for some playoff games, which could have hurt his relationship with the team. This winter, or whenever the lockout ends, Chisholm will have the opportunity to choose where he wants to play. However, he has made it clear that he wants to stay in New York. “Chisholm, an All-Star for the second time in 2025, endured a down year at the plate and struggled both offensively and defensively in four appearances in the playoffs. Manager Aaron Boone left Chisholm out of the Yankees' starting lineup for two postseason games, including their season-ending loss on Wednesday. The fans at Yankee Stadium booed Chisholm after he fouled out to first base as a pinch hitter in the bottom of the seventh inning. Nevertheless, Chisholm would rather continue his career with the Yankees than exit in free agency," MLB Trade Rumors' wrote. If Chisholm decides not to return to New York, Bleacher Report's Zachary D. Rymer believes he should sign with the San Diego Padres . “Starting pitching will need to be a priority, but another bat should also be a must. The Padres specifically need more left-handed thump after getting just a .385 SLG from that side of the plate. They could also use more offensive production at second base, where Jake Cronenworth struggled in 2026. Also, does anyone else get the sense that San Diego would be a good spot for Chisholm's energy? He plays with a chip on his shoulder, and that's been the Padres' whole vibe as they have fought the Los Angeles Dodgers for control of the NL West throughout the 2020,” Rymer wrote. A move to San Diego could be an exciting opportunity for Chisholm, who would bring the kind of energy that fits with the rest of the organization. Seeing Chisholm and Fernando Tatis Jr. on the same team would be an intriguing possibility. Chisholm played on a $10 million contract with the Yankees last season. He also won a Silver Slugger not too long ago, adding to his appeal as a potential addition. San Diego could be an ideal fit for Chisholm and his energetic style of play. Rymer believes he should sign with the San Diego Padres . “Starting pitching will need to be a priority, but another bat should also be a must. The Padres specifically need more left-handed thump after getting just a .385 SLG from that side of the plate. They could also use more offensive production at second base, where Jake Cronenworth struggled in 2026. Also, does anyone else get the sense that San Diego would be a good spot for Chisholm's energy? He plays with a chip on his shoulder, and that's been the Padres' whole vibe as they have fought the Los Angeles Dodgers for control of the NL West throughout the 2020,” Rymer wrote. A move to San Diego could be an exciting opportunity for Chisholm, who would bring the kind of energy that fits with the rest of the organization. Seeing Chisholm and Fernando Tatis Jr. on the same team would be an intriguing possibility. Chisholm played on a $10 million contract with the Yankees last season. He also won a Silver Slugger not too long ago, adding to his appeal as a potential addition. San Diego could be an ideal fit for Chisholm and his energetic style of play. item.title: FG approves 4 new channel management firms for seaports
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Federal Executive Council (FEC) has approved four new channel management companies for seaports across the country in a move aimed at improving vessel navigation and port operations. Speaking at the recently concluded Annual General Meeting of the Nigerian Association of Master Mariners (NAMM), former General Manager, Marine and Operations, Capt. Ebubeogu Ihenacho, disclosed that there would be changes in the ownership of the Lagos Channel Management Company Limited and the Bonny Channel Management Company. Although Vanguard could not independently ascertain the identities of the new owners, sources close to the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) said a Belgian company is expected to take over channel management operations at the Lagos ports. According to Ihenacho, the four channels serving Nigeria’s major port clusters will have different channel management companies as approved by the FEC. He said a new company had been approved to manage the Lagos port channel, with a change of name, while the Calabar Channel would be managed by the Calabar Channel Management Company. He added that the Bonny Channel Management Company had also undergone a change of ownership. On the Warri Channel, Ihenacho said the Federal Government had approved China Harbour Engineering Company (CHEC) and two other companies to form a consortium to manage the Escravos Channel. He said: “For Warri, it was approved for China Harbour Engineering Company, CHEC, and two other companies, who would now form a consortium. That consortium will now form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) with the Nigerian Ports Authority to manage the Escravos Channel.” Recall that the management of the NPA had declined to renew the concessions of the Lagos Channel Management Company Limited and the Bonny Channel Management Company, opting instead for six-month extensions of the existing arrangements. The post FG approves 4 new channel management firms for seaports appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Landing cost of petrol falls to N1,283.81/litre
item.description: •As crude oil rises to $108.90 per barrel By Ediri Ejoh The landing cost of imported Premium Motor Spirit, PMS, also known as petrol, has dropped marginally to N1,283.81 per litre from N1,292.88 per litre. The latest figure was disclosed by the Major Energies Marketers Association of Nigeria, MEMAN, in its energy bulletin yesterday. The decline came as Brent crude rose marginally to $108.90 per barrel from $108.80 per barrel, according to figures contained in the report. The latest landing cost is N66.19, or about 4.90 per cent, below Dangote Refinery’s gantry price of N1,350 per litre. Similarly, the landing cost of imported petrol was between N64.19 and N74.19 per litre below the ex-depot prices of N1,348 to N1,358 quoted by depot owners. Despite the decline in landing cost, petrol prices remained elevated in parts of the country, with motorists in Lagos and Abuja reportedly paying between N1,370 and N1,429 per litre at filling stations. The difference between landing costs and pump prices reflects additional costs and margins across the supply chain, including transportation, storage and retail operations. The development comes amid the Federal Government’s proposed 30-day petrol discount at NNPC Limited filling stations. Recall that the Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, on October 8 proposed that petrol be sold at N1,350 per litre at NNPC Limited outlets under the planned discount initiative. However, the proposed discount had yet to be implemented at NNPC Limited filling stations as of the time of reporting. The post Landing cost of petrol falls to N1,283.81/litre appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Atiku lacks expertise to fix Nigeria’s economy — APC National Secretary
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ajibola Bashiru, has questioned former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s expertise to fix Nigeria’s economy, saying President Bola Tinubu is addressing the country’s economic challenges while predicting that Nigerians will reject Atiku in the 2027 presidential election. Bashiru spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, while responding to questions about Atiku’s political ambitions and whether the former vice-president poses a threat to the ruling party ahead of the 2027 general election. “Atiku is not a professional, please, with respect to him. Atiku trained as an hygiene expert at the school of hygiene in Kano, He is a ‘wole wole’ man and went to be a tax collector in Customs. Where is the expertise? What has he done? Check his profile?” Bashiru said. He argued that holding the office of vice-president did not automatically make Atiku an expert on the economy. “So, the fact that you became a Vice President doesn’t make you an expert, what is his expertise?” he asked. Bashiru also linked Atiku to the economic difficulties the Tinubu administration is addressing, arguing that the former vice-president was among those responsible for the challenges facing the country. “If there are challenges that is being addressed by President Tinubu, one of the main people that caused it is Atiku Abubakar,” he said. Asked whether Atiku posed a threat to the APC, Bashiru described the former vice-president’s latest presidential ambition as his final attempt, predicting that Nigerians would reject him. “Atiku is the Oginga Odinga of our country and that is what the Vice president said. He is doing his last contest which he knows that Nigeria people would reject him because Atiku you mentioned cannot even come to talk about Nigerian economy,” he said. The APC national secretary also criticised opposition figures making promises about reducing petrol prices, arguing that such claims were unrealistic and intended to win votes. “You see, some of these people can just come to make statements. I learnt one of them said I’m going to make petrol 200 naira, 300 naira. It is not possible, he is just lying. You must not lie to people because you want to get their votes. You must even say something that is even realistic,” Bashiru added. The post 2027: Atiku lacks expertise to fix Nigeria’s economy — APC National Secretary appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Insurance firms’ N300b stuck at CBN over verification for illicit funds
item.description: By Rosemary Iwunze Insurance companies are now struggling to have access to the new capital they raised, amounting to about N300 billion under the just concluded recapitalization programme. The funds were held in the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, pending verifications for illicit funds inflows. Vanguard learnt that following suspicion of possible illicit sources of some of the new investments in the firms the apex imposed stricter capital verification regime, a development which has proved tough for most of the insurance firms to scale through. It is further learnt that while the National Insurance Commission, NAICOM, has given approval for the apex bank to release the funds to the insurers, the affected firms are painstakingly going through the processes. Speaking to journalist during the virtual press briefing on the outcome of the Insurers Committee meeting, Chairman of Nigeria Insurers Association, NIA, Mrs. Ebelechukwu Nwachukwu, stated that, the insurance sector regulator has done its part while operators are currently working on the CBN criteria to access the funds on or before the end of this month. The insurers said they had planned to deploy the new capital in the third quarter of this year to boost their financial performance in 2026 while rewarding their investors with good returns in dividend for their support in the recapitalization program. Recall that the 24 insurance companies had cumulatively raised N300 billion during the exercise, added to over N700 billion existing capital, taking the total industry capital to N1.079 trillion, post recapitalisation. The Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act (NIIRA), 2025, had stipulated that the underwriting firms and reinsurers who participated in the recapitalisation exercise that ended on July 31st, 2026 must keep their recapitalised funds in an escrow account with CBN. Of the 50 firms that scaled through the recapitalisation hurdle, 24 of them raised fresh capital while 26 of them had earlier surpassed the minimum capital benchmark. NIIRA had mandated life underwriters to recapitalise from N2billion to N10billion, non-life from N3billion to N15billion while reinsurers were required to upgrade from N10billion to N35billion. The Commissioner for Insurance/CEO, NAICOM, Mr. Olusegun Omosehin, had earlier disclosed that the capital in the market has now risen to N1.079trillion, up from about N700billion before the exercise. According to him, NAICOM now wants to allow operators access the recapitalisation funds, he promised that the regulator would monitor the operators to ensure that the funds fulfill its purpose and not mismanaged or divested into something else. The post Insurance firms’ N300b stuck at CBN over verification for illicit funds appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Stop reacting, start protecting: Inside Nigeria’s fight to keep children safe in schools
item.description: By Adesina Wahab, Elizabeth Osayande & Ifunanya Ndigwe When a child leaves home in the morning with a school bag strapped to his back, the unspoken promise is simple: he will learn, grow, and return home safely. In Nigeria today, that promise is broken too often. •From left, President, All Nigeria Confederation of Principals of Secondary Schools (ANCOPSS), Lagos State, Mr. Olushola Masheyi walls,” she said.By 2021, the Ministry of Finance (representing ANCOPSS National President, Dr Robert Okorie); Executive Director, Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism, convened a high-level meeting Mrs Alaka; Chairman, Education Writers’ Association of Nigeria (EWAN), Mr. Mojeed Alabi; Lagos State Police Commissioner, Mr Fatai with Defence, Police, DSS, Office Tijani (representing Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu); National Coordinator, Financing Safe Schools in Nigeria, Hajia Haliof the National Security Adviser, ma Iliya and Chairman, Nigeria Union of Teachers, Lagos State Wing, Comrade Hassan Akintoye (representing NUT National President, Mr. Titus Amba) at the 2026 EWAN National Summit on School Safety in Lagos From Chibok in 2014 where schoolgirls were taken from their dormitories, to Dapchi, to Oriire in Oyo State, to corps members attacked in Imo, to classrooms emptied by sit-at-home order in the South-East and farmer-herder clashes in Benue, Oyo and Ogun – the classroom has become a frontline. It was against this sobering reality that journalists, security chiefs, government officials, teachers and principals converged on Ikeja, Lagos, for the 7th Annual Summit of the Education Writers Association of Nigeria, EWAN. The theme was deliberate and urgent: School Under Threat: From Reactive Responses to Sustainable Protection. Chairing the summit was the Chairman, Governing Board of the National Universities Commission, NUC, Prof. Oluwatoyin Ogundipe, represented by Prof. Joseph Awoyinfa. The keynote, on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu, was delivered by the Lagos State Commissioner of Police, Mr. Fatai Tijani. But beyond titles and protocol, the message was one: Nigeria must stop waiting for the next abduction before it acts. The Chairperson’s Warning: Don’t stop at the press statement. Prof. Ogundipe, as chairperson, set the tone. He did not want another conference of communiques. He challenged education journalists to change the way school safety is reported. “When authorities announce new security measures, our reporting should not end with the announcement. When funds are allocated, we should investigate whether they are used as intended, and when investigations produce recommendations, we should return to determine what has changed,” he said. “Our ultimate objective is not to embarrass institutions. It is to ensure that they fulfil their responsibilities.” For a country where security votes and intervention funds often disappear into vague budget lines, it was a pointed call for accountability journalism
item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Adesina Wahab, Elizabeth Osayande & Ifunanya Ndigwe When a child leaves home in the morning with a school bag strapped to his back, the unspoken promise is simple: he will learn, grow, and return home safely. In Nigeria today, that promise is broken too often. •From left, President, All Nigeria Confederation of Principals of Secondary Schools (ANCOPSS), Lagos State, Mr. Olushola Masheyi walls,” she said.By 2021, the Ministry of Finance (representing ANCOPSS National President, Dr Robert Okorie); Executive Director, Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism, convened a high-level meeting Mrs Alaka; Chairman, Education Writers’ Association of Nigeria (EWAN), Mr. Mojeed Alabi; Lagos State Police Commissioner, Mr Fatai with Defence, Police, DSS, Office Tijani (representing Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu); National Coordinator, Financing Safe Schools in Nigeria, Hajia Haliof the National Security Adviser, ma Iliya and Chairman, Nigeria Union of Teachers, Lagos State Wing, Comrade Hassan Akintoye (representing NUT National President, Mr. Titus Amba) at the 2026 EWAN National Summit on School Safety in Lagos From Chibok in 2014 where schoolgirls were taken from their dormitories, to Dapchi, to Oriire in Oyo State, to corps members attacked in Imo, to classrooms emptied by sit-at-home order in the South-East and farmer-herder clashes in Benue, Oyo and Ogun – the classroom has become a frontline. It was against this sobering reality that journalists, security chiefs, government officials, teachers and principals converged on Ikeja, Lagos, for the 7th Annual Summit of the Education Writers Association of Nigeria, EWAN. The theme was deliberate and urgent: School Under Threat: From Reactive Responses to Sustainable Protection. Chairing the summit was the Chairman, Governing Board of the National Universities Commission, NUC, Prof. Oluwatoyin Ogundipe, represented by Prof. Joseph Awoyinfa. The keynote, on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu, was delivered by the Lagos State Commissioner of Police, Mr. Fatai Tijani. But beyond titles and protocol, the message was one: Nigeria must stop waiting for the next abduction before it acts. The Chairperson’s Warning: Don’t stop at the press statement. Prof. Ogundipe, as chairperson, set the tone. He did not want another conference of communiques. He challenged education journalists to change the way school safety is reported. “When authorities announce new security measures, our reporting should not end with the announcement. When funds are allocated, we should investigate whether they are used as intended, and when investigations produce recommendations, we should return to determine what has changed,” he said. “Our ultimate objective is not to embarrass institutions. It is to ensure that they fulfil their responsibilities.” For a country where security votes and intervention funds often disappear into vague budget lines, it was a pointed call for accountability journalism. “Children are not safe until every school is safe” If Ogundipe gave the framework, EWAN Chairman, Mojeed Alabi, gave the conscience. Standing before his colleagues, Alabi began with a line that would echo through the hall all day: Children are not safe until every school is safe. “No parent should have to choose between a child’s education and their safety. No teacher should have to teach under the shadow of abduction, and no community should have to watch its future disappear because its schools have become targets,” he said. In a deeply personal address titled: Why Journalism Matters in the Fight Against Violent Attacks on Schools, Alabi traced the pattern Nigerians have come to know too well: an attack happens, government issues a statement, security agencies announce interventions, public outrage rises, then attention moves elsewhere – until the next attack. “We must therefore ask: how many more warnings, disrupted school terms and grieving families will it take before school safety becomes an unquestionable national priority?” he asked. His answer was journalism that makes the invisible visible. Not just reporting the number of children abducted, but asking whether the school had a functional emergency response system. Whether teachers had safety training. Whether there was a channel to report threats. How many school days were lost. Whether survivors returned to school. What support they got. “Behind every school attack are human lives. Children must never be reduced to statistics or used merely to provoke sympathy. Their stories deserve accuracy, dignity, sensitivity and appropriate protection of their identities,” Alabi said. “We cannot promise that journalism alone will end attacks on schools but journalism can ensure that warning signs are not ignored, public resources are scrutinised, failures are exposed, promises are tracked and affected communities are heard.” It was a call for newsrooms to invest in expertise, collaborate with researchers, and use radio, television, newspapers and digital platforms to reach communities often excluded from national conversations. The IGP’s Question: How can a child learn in fear? When CP Fatai Tijani rose to deliver the IGP’s keynote, he came with a question that silenced the room. “How can a child concentrate on learning when the fear of violence, abduction or other security threats is constantly present?” For IGP Tunji Disu, school safety is no longer a peripheral police duty it is national security. He outlined four pillars: intelligence-led policing and early warning, stronger police-community partnerships, improved preparedness and coordinated response, and professionalism with respect for human rights. And he had a warning for journalists too: “The need for speed in journalism must never displace the obligation to accuracy.” Sensational headlines, he said, can compromise rescue efforts and endanger children. The $15 Billion Question: Where did the money go? One of the most revealing sessions came from Hajia Halima Iliya, National Coordinator, Financing Safe Schools in Nigeria during the panel discussion. She took the audience back to the beginning how the Safe Schools Initiative was launched to enable victims to continue education unhindered, how persistent attacks forced Nigeria to sign the Safe Schools Declaration in 2019 alongside over 100 countries, mostly from the Sahel region and West Africa. “There is more to what we are seeing which requires collective collaboration. Some of the actors are cross-border actors. They pass through the land, through the walls,” she said. By 2021, the Ministry of Finance convened a high-level meeting with Defence, Police, DSS, Office of the National Security Adviser, Ministry of Education, NSCDC, governors, EU and World Bank. The verdict: Nigeria had no mid-term expenditure framework for school safety. “Under my leadership, we developed a national plan on financing safe schools 2023-2026. By 2022, this document was developed and was launched. We started full implementation in 2023, with the Federal Government releasing N15 billion to the implementing regions,” she disclosed. A database of vulnerable communities was built with CSOs, a National Safe Schools Response Centre established, and hunters, vigilante and forest guards trained within community ecosystems. Lagos and Jigawa, she said, have become champions. “Over 4,000 students were trained across four states last year,” she said, with technology deployed to communities without network and hardware for the Police Schools Protection Squad. Her plea: Governors must embed Safe Schools into annual budgets. Without a budget, there can be no sustainable protection. Fencing, data and a weak justice system The panel also brought the conversation down from policy to the school gate. Comrade Hassan Akintoye, Chairman, NUT Lagos Wing, representing the NUT National President, was blunt: school threat has always been around, but today it

item.title: Ebola: Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for the N10 billion announced for Ebola preparedness, alleging that the confirmed case in Abuja exposed serious gaps in surveillance and the protection of health workers. Atiku said the government must explain how the emergency funds were spent and why the response allegedly left frontline health workers without adequate protective equipment. He also warned against using the outbreak to restrict political campaigns and voter participation. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, on Wednesday, Atiku demanded a public audit of the funds and answers over the handling of the case. “Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered. A press statement cannot replace an audit,” he said. Atiku said the patient arrived in Nigeria on October 5, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, but the government did not publicly confirm the case until October 20. “During that critical period, 44 close contacts were left unmonitored, while private health workers faced the case without adequate protective equipment. This is a failure of preparedness with potentially grave consequences,” he said. He also questioned the Presidential Task Force announced by Tinubu in June and chaired by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, insisting that medical experts should lead the response. “Political titles cannot trace contacts, equip hospitals or save lives,” Atiku said. The former vice president further alleged that the planned press conference by the Minister of Health on Thursday was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies and voting. “The Tinubu administration must not weaponise Ebola to frighten the public, silence its opponents or suppress voter participation. Any public health measure must be backed by clear medical evidence, applied equally and never used as a pretext to interfere with Nigerians’ democratic rights,” he said. Atiku urged the government to account for the N10 billion, protect health workers and trace all contacts, warning against turning a public health emergency into a tool for political suppression. item.title: AI firms say UK has a year to head off datacentre protests before construction is threatened
item.description: Exclusive: Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco taskforce urges ministers to offer areas greater benefits from tech infrastructure amid fears of US-style opposition AI companies have told ministers they have 12 months to head off public opposition to datacentres in the UK or risk US-style protests that could threaten their construction. Successive dry summers and rising energy bills are increasing public scrutiny of plans for the huge computer warehouses that are used to train and run AI models, says a submission to the Labour government from a group including the AI infrastructure companies Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco. Continue reading...

item.title: Poor Network: Reps give MTN, Airtel, Glo, Mafab seven days
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives Ad Hoc Committee investigating the persistent poor quality of telecommunications services in Nigeria has given the chief executive officers of MTN, Airtel, Globacom, Mafab Communications and other operators seven days to appear before it. The committee directed the telecom executives to appear on October 28, 2026, to explain the persistent deterioration in network quality and their failure to honour previous invitations. The ultimatum was issued at a public hearing in Abuja on Wednesday following the adoption of two motions sponsored by Reps. Sunday Umeha and Afam Ogene. The lawmakers expressed displeasure over the failure of invited operators, including MTN Nigeria and Mafab Communications, to appear before the committee as previously requested. Consequently, the committee directed the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) to ensure that all affected operators comply with the invitation and appear at 2 p.m. on October 28 at Hearing Room 447 of the New Building of the National Assembly Complex, Abuja. The operators were also directed to submit all relevant documents to the committee on or before the scheduled date and explain the factors responsible for the persistent decline in service quality affecting millions of subscribers and businesses nationwide. The lawmakers warned that any chief executive who failed to honour the invitation could face a possible arrest summons to compel their appearance. Speaking at the hearing, the committee chairman, Rep. Olumide Osoba (APC, Ogun), said reliable telecommunications services had become critical to Nigeria’s economy, extending beyond voice calls and internet access to essential commercial activities, including Point of Sale (POS) transactions. Osoba noted that businesses, financial transactions and other essential services depended heavily on reliable telecommunications networks, making recurring service disruptions a matter of serious national concern. He said the House constituted the ad hoc committee to investigate persistent complaints by subscribers and establish the factors responsible for the poor quality of services provided by telecommunications operators. The chairman, however, expressed concern that the invited chief executives had continued to avoid direct engagement with the committee by offering various excuses or sending lower-ranking officials to represent them. He stressed that the committee expected the chief executives to appear personally, noting that they were better positioned to explain their companies’ operational challenges and commitments to improving service delivery. Also speaking, Rep. Ibe Osonwa criticised the operators for what he described as disregard for the House, despite the substantial revenue they generated from their operations in Nigeria. The committee directed the telecom executives to appear on October 28, 2026, to explain the persistent deterioration in network quality and their failure to honour previous invitations. The ultimatum was issued at a public hearing in Abuja on Wednesday following the adoption of two motions sponsored by Reps. Sunday Umeha and Afam Ogene. The lawmakers expressed displeasure over the failure of invited operators, including MTN Nigeria and Mafab Communications, to appear before the committee as previously requested. Consequently, the committee directed the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) to ensure that all affected operators comply with the invitation and appear at 2 p.m. on October 28 at Hearing Room 447 of the New Building of the National Assembly Complex, Abuja. The operators were also directed to submit all relevant documents to the committee on or before the scheduled date and explain the factors responsible for the persistent decline in service quality affecting millions of subscribers and businesses nationwide. The lawmakers warned that any chief executive who failed to honour the invitation could face a possible arrest summons to compel their appearance. Speaking at the hearing, the committee chairman, Rep. Olumide Osoba (APC, Ogun), said reliable telecommunications services had become critical to Nigeria’s economy, extending beyond voice calls and internet access to essential commercial activities, including Point of Sale (POS) transactions. Osoba noted that businesses, financial transactions and other essential services depended heavily on reliable telecommunications networks, making recurring service disruptions a matter of serious national concern. He said the House constituted the ad hoc committee to investigate persistent complaints by subscribers and establish the factors responsible for the poor quality of services provided by telecommunications operators. The chairman, however, expressed concern that the invited chief executives had continued to avoid direct engagement with the committee by offering various excuses or sending lower-ranking officials to represent them. He stressed that the committee expected the chief executives to appear personally, noting that they were better positioned to explain their companies’ operational challenges and commitments to improving service delivery. Also speaking, Rep. Ibe Osonwa criticised the operators for what he described as disregard for the House, despite the substantial revenue they generated from their operations in Nigeria. Osonwa said it was unacceptable for companies benefiting from the Nigerian market to ignore legislative invitations, particularly when lawmakers sought explanations on issues directly affecting their customers and the wider economy. He maintained that telecommunications operators had a responsibility to account for the quality of services delivered to Nigerians, warning that the House would not overlook attempts to frustrate its investigation. In his ruling, Osoba urged the NCC to ensure full compliance with the committee’s directive, reiterating that the affected operators must appear on October 28 with the required documents and explanations on the state of their networks. item.title: Ebola patient arrived Abuja Oct. 3 via Ethiopian Airlines from Uganda – Source
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Fresh facts emerged, yesterday, regarding the travel itinerary of the confirmed Ebola virus patient in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, revealing that the index case entered Nigeria aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight earlier this month. Read Also: No vaccine, specific treatment for Ebola strain in Nigeria — WHO A highly-placed aviation official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, as she was not authorised to brief the media on the matter, told Vanguard that the patient arrived in the country on October 3, 2026. This is even as the Ugandan government asked Nigeria to provide detailed travel and clinical records of the woman, the index case, insisting she didn’t pick the virus in its territory, since there is no Ebola case in Uganda. According to the aviation official, the patient landed at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, aboard Ethiopian Airlines Flight ET333. The revelation provides critical details for contact-tracing, following an earlier official announcement by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Pate, who confirmed the presence of the virus in the nation’s capital. Pate had disclosed that the female patient had recently returned to Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda and subsequently spent several days receiving care at a private hospital in Abuja before the infection was formally diagnosed. She has since been transferred to a designated isolation facility where she is currently receiving treatment. In response, a multi-agency operation involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, and the FCT Health and Environmental Services Secretariat has commenced extensive contact-tracing. Public health authorities have so far identified 44 close contacts, including healthcare personnel, fellow hospital patients, caregivers and individuals connected to her travel route. Consequently, the Federal Government has placed health institutions and port health surveillance units across the country on high alert. Vanguard News The post Ebola patient arrived Abuja Oct. 3 via Ethiopian Airlines from Uganda – Source appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: IBM CEO says open weight models are now irresistibly good and cheap on-prem
item.description: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna has told investors that open weight models now make brilliant sense for on-prem enterprise use. Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Krishna said that in 2024 closed frontier models were plainly superior to open alternatives. “If you ran some assessment, some benchmark, and it was broad-based, not narrow, the top model might score a 70, and the open model might score a 20 or a 30.” “In late 2025, we began to see that gap shrink, where maybe the gap was not 70 to 20 or 30, it was 70 to 50,” he continued. The CEO said open weight models currently deliver “anywhere from 25 percent to 10 percent of the token cost of the frontier models. That is very attractive given that they’re now 90 percent as effective.” “It’s a simple question for any enterprise. Would you like something that’s 10 percent of the cost if it’s 90 percent as good as the best, or do you want to pay that 10 times higher cost?” Krishna thinks businesses will most often choose not to incur the higher costs. “Then the question is: how many tasks require that? I would tell you some do, but the vast majority, summarizing an email, examining a contract, answering a customer call, composing an email, all of those can be done as well with the much cheaper answer.” The CEO said those numbers mean IBM is seeing booming interest in on-prem AI infrastructure. While he thinks most businesses can build useful AI infrastructure in just two or three racks, he feels many will struggle to get it running. “The question becomes: how do you do that?” he said. “The question that the enterprise struggles with is: ‘Where are my kernel engineers? Where are the people who worry about the underlying network? Who can make sure that the model is clustered on GPUs that are close to each other in network proximity? Who can make sure that you’re doing the right caching of results so you get an incredible response?’” He didn’t have answers, other than to say IBM will produce software that eases AI deployments. Krishna also predicted demand for on-prem AI will spur sales of Big Blue’s Spyre mainframe accelerator cards. The CEO said current-gen z17 mainframes have delivered $1bn more revenue than any previous model, and said Big Blue’s new rackable models delivered “the strongest midrange launch in IBM Z in nearly two decades.” Mainframe revenue, however, fell 20 percent – as IBM expects given it’s now 18 months since it launched the z17. IBM’s infrastructure revenue grew five percent year-over-year to $3.7 billion, much slower improvement than recorded by rivals Dell, HPE, and Lenovo. Software did rather better, scoring nine percent growth to reach $7.8 billion for the quarter. Red Hat was the star, growing eleven percent and increasing annual recurring revenue by 30 percent. Some of that future revenue is for Red Hat’s virtualization products, which have now won $800 million of deals, with a pipeline of a further $750 million. Where are the people who worry about the underlying network? Who can make sure that the model is clustered on GPUs that are close to each other in network proximity? Who can make sure that you’re doing the right caching of results so you get an incredible response?’” He didn’t have answers, other than to say IBM will produce software that eases AI deployments. Krishna also predicted demand for on-prem AI will spur sales of Big Blue’s Spyre mainframe accelerator cards. The CEO said current-gen z17 mainframes have delivered $1bn more revenue than any previous model, and said Big Blue’s new rackable models delivered “the strongest midrange launch in IBM Z in nearly two decades.” Mainframe revenue, however, fell 20 percent – as IBM expects given it’s now 18 months since it launched the z17. IBM’s infrastructure revenue grew five percent year-over-year to $3.7 billion, much slower improvement than recorded by rivals Dell, HPE, and Lenovo. Software did rather better, scoring nine percent growth to reach $7.8 billion for the quarter. Red Hat was the star, growing eleven percent and increasing annual recurring revenue by 30 percent. Some of that future revenue is for Red Hat’s virtualization products, which have now won $800 million of deals, with a pipeline of a further $750 million. That’s a solid result for a product line launched in 2024, and IBM believes there’s more to come given the possibility some VMware users are on the move. Total quarterly revenue hit $17.1 billion, up five percent. IBM’s share price wobbled in after-hours trading and ended down a point or two. ‘Emergency maintenance’ for IBM Cloud Another IBM matter The Register is watching today is a severity one incident in the Big Blue cloud, caused by “emergency maintenance” that meant users could not provision new resources or virtual private clouds for 90 minutes. Users of IBM’s Classic Cloud, the service it acquired from SoftLayer in 2013, have been told Big Blue will “restore new provisioning and resource management in our Classic environment” by 08:00 UTC on Thursday – meaning the incident will last at least 16 hours. IBM commenced that work a handful of hours after the announcement of critical bugs in PHP . We’ve asked if fixing that flaw is the reason for the incident and will update this story if we get a response. ®

item.content:encoded: •Ebola patient arrived Abuja Oct. 3 via Ethiopian Airlines from Uganda – Source *Nigeria confirms first Ebola case is Bundibugyo strain *Uganda seeks details of Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola case *Nigeria, Uganda collaborating to contain Ebola — FG *Senate, Reps ask FG to make screening mandatory for passengers at all entry points, borders Urge govt to release emergency funds from service-wide votes to relevant agencies to curb disease *To immediately amend Quarantine Act of 1926 By Sola Ogundipe, Health Editor , Henry Umoru, Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Omeiza Ajayi, Luminous Jannamike & Gift Odekina ABUJA — Fresh facts emerged yesterday regarding the travel itinerary of the confirmed Ebola virus patient in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, revealing that the index case entered Nigeria aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight earlier this month. A highly-placed aviation official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, as she was not authorised to brief the media on the matter, told Vanguard that the patient arrived in the country on October 3, 2026. This came on a day an emergency meeting of officials of the health ministry revealed the index case detected in the country carried the Bundibugyo strain of the virus which, according to the World Health Organisation, WHO, has no vaccine or specific treatment. This is even as the Ugandan government asked Nigeria to provide detailed travel and clinical records of the woman, the index case, insisting she didn’t pick the virus in its territory, since there is no Ebola case in Uganda. Meanwhile, the two arms of the National Assembly, Senate and House of Representatives, have asked the Federal Government to urgently release money to relevant agencies to confront the disease. According to the aviation official, the patient landed at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, aboard Ethiopian Airlines Flight ET333. The revelation provides critical details for contact-tracing, following an earlier official announcement by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Pate, who confirmed the presence of the virus in the nation’s capital. Pate had disclosed that the female patient had recently returned to Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda and subsequently spent several days receiving care at a private hospital in Abuja before the infection was formally diagnosed. She has since been transferred to a designated isolation facility where she is currently receiving treatment. In response, a multi-agency operation involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, and the FCT Health and Environmental Services Secretariat has commenced extensive contact-tracing. Public health authorities have so far identified 44 close contacts, including healthcare personnel, fellow hospital patients, caregivers and individuals connected to her travel route. Consequently, the Federal Government has placed health institutions and port health surveillance units across the country on high alert. Nigeria confirms first Ebola case is Bundibugyo strain The first Ebola case detected in Nigeria is the Bundibugyo strain, an emergency meeting on the issue was told yesterday. “We did three levels of tests, but all molecular. The strain was Bundibugyo,” Olajumoke Babatunde, Director of the Public Health Laboratory Service at NCDC, said yesterday. The World Health Organization, WHO, which also confirmed that it was the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment. “This person is actually a diplomat,” another official said, adding the patient had deteriorated into “multi-organ failure”. The official did not disclose the nationality of the diplomat. In August, Uganda was declared officially Ebola-free by WHO after recording 20 cases, almost all people who had travelled from the DRC. Uganda seeks details of Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola case In a related development, Uganda has asked Nigeria to provide detailed travel and clinical records of the index case in the country. The Federal Government had confirmed on Tuesday that the woman recently arrived in Nigeria after travelling from Uganda. But in a statement, Director-General of Health Services, Uganda Ministry of Health, Prof. Charles Olaro, said the information is required to guide further investigations and determine whether additional contact-tracing was necessary, even as he stressed that the woman’s transit through Uganda did not establish that she contracted the virus there. The statement, issued in Kampala, said the Ministry of Health is awaiting further information from the Nigerian government to help establish the circumstances surrounding the infection, adding that it would strengthen screening and other public health measures at points of entry in collaboration with relevant agencies. Preliminary information cited by the Ugandan authorities revealed that the woman, who travelled to the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo for business, transited through Uganda in early October without showing symptoms, but reportedly developed symptoms after arriving in Nigeria, as the location where she contracted the virus remained under investigation. The statement, titled “Reported Ebola Case in Nigeria: Ministry Calls for Calm and Vigilance” read: “The Ministry of Health has noted reports of a confirmed Ebola case in Nigeria involving a Nigerian woman who reportedly travelled to the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo for business. “Preliminary information indicates that she transited through Uganda in early October without showing symptoms and developed symptoms after arriving in Nigeria. Her transit through Uganda does not establish that she contracted the infection there. The location of exposure remains under investigation. “The government of Nigeria is yet to provide detailed information on the woman’s travel itinerary and clinical history to guide further investigations and any necessary contact tracing. “The ministry wishes to clarify that, as of the date of this statement, Uganda has no confirmed active Ebola cases.” It said limited provisions had been maintained to facilitate humanitarian and diplomatic movements. Senate asks FG to make screening mandatory for passengers at all international airports, others. Nigeria, Uganda collaborating to contain Ebola — FG But the federal government said yesterday it was collaborating with Uganda to contain the risk of the disease outbreak, assuring Nigerians that public health authorities were coordinating response measures. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this while fielding questions from journalists after a meeting at the Office of the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila. Pate was asked to react to reports that Ugandan authorities had said there was no Ebola case in their country, despite reports that a Nigerian woman had contracted the virus in Uganda. He said Nigeria was working with the East African country, while taking steps to contain the reported case and prevent further transmission. “All I can tell you is that we are collaborating with our sister African nation of Uganda. What is important is that we have found this one case. We are doing contact tracing, and we are putting containment measures to ensure that it doesn’t go into our population,” the minister said. Pate said Nigeria had competent public health institutions capable of responding to the situation, citing the country’s experience in managing the 2014 Ebola outbreak. “We have done it in 2014, and we have good public health institutions,” he said. He urged Nigerians to remain vigilant but avoid panic, advising the public to rely on information from trusted public health authorities rather than circulate unverified reports. “Nigerians should be reassured. item.title: APOD: 2026 October 22 – The First Green Star, WD J1330+6435
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 22 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The First Green Star, WD J1330+6435 Explanation: Star light, star bright: is there a green star out tonight? Other than the Sun , all stars are so far from Earth that they appear as points in the sky. They are mostly white, but sometimes noticeably red or blue . This color typically relates to the temperature: blue stars are hotter than red stars. What about other colors? The featured image is an illustration showing WD J1330+6435 , a white dwarf star , surrounded by an accretion disk with gas and rocks orbiting the star. White dwarfs are small, faint stars that are left over when a star like the Sun exhausts its nuclear fuel . Astronomers recently found that some white dwarf stars, despite their name, would appear yellow, green, cyan, pink, or purple . In these cases , trace elements that were accreted to these stars interact with the stellar atmosphere and shift its normally white color. But, alas! I wish I may, I wish I might, but they are too faint to see tonight … Tomorrow’s picture: eye in the sky Date October 22, 2026 Credit & Copyright Mark A. item.title: Where to find all ancient equipment in Final Fantasy Resonance

You can upgrade the ancient items into some of the best equips in the game , provided you can take on a few tough enemies.

But in September and October 2026, as drought gripped New Guinea (sometimes called Papua) amid a strong El Niño , fires scorched the island and smoke shrouded large swaths of it for weeks. The VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) on the NOAA-20 satellite captured this image of thick smoke streaming from the southern part of the island on October 11, 2026. In recent weeks, soaring levels of air pollution delayed and canceled flights , closed schools, and prompted officials in some areas to urge children and older people to wear masks. “Sometimes smoke that has drifted into the convection of nearby thunderstorms will get washed out or lofted up into the upper troposphere, but a lot of smoke stays near the surface and causes air quality problems,” said Robert Field, an associate research scientist at NASA’s Goddard Institute for Space Studies and Columbia University. “It’s a horrible situation.” According to the Global Fire Emissions Database (GFED), a fire emissions monitoring system, fires in Papua New Guinea, on the eastern half of the island, had released nearly 32 megatons of carbon by October 19, more than any other year on record at that point in the year. “Emissions are already much higher than the 2015 total for the year, and it’s very likely that this will become the highest year on record for Papua New Guinea, even surpassing 1997,” said Guido van der Werf, a fire scientist at Wageningen University & Research. On the Indonesian side, sometimes called West New Guinea or Indonesian Papua, carbon emissions exceeded 35 megatons , the third highest after 2015 and 1997, other El Niño years with severe fires. Van der Werf led the development of GFED, a satellite-driven modeling framework that uses a mix of remote sensing , vegetation characteristics, and other information to estimate the extent of vegetation fires and the emissions over nearly three decades. item.content:encoded: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Fires Char New Guinea Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search New Guinea, the world’s second-largest island, harbors an extraordinary variety of plant life across more than a dozen distinct ecoregions , including seasonally dry savannas, tropical rainforests, and lowland swamp forests. But in September and October 2026, as drought gripped New Guinea (sometimes called Papua) amid a strong El Niño , fires scorched the island and smoke shrouded large swaths of it for weeks. The VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) on the NOAA-20 satellite captured this image of thick smoke streaming from the southern part of the island on October 11, 2026. In recent weeks, soaring levels of air pollution delayed and canceled flights , closed schools, and prompted officials in some areas to urge children and older people to wear masks. “Sometimes smoke that has drifted into the convection of nearby thunderstorms will get washed out or lofted up into the upper troposphere, but a lot of smoke stays near the surface and causes air quality problems,” said Robert Field, an associate research scientist at NASA’s Goddard Institute for Space Studies and Columbia University. “It’s a horrible situation.” According to the Global Fire Emissions Database (GFED), a fire emissions monitoring system, fires in Papua New Guinea, on the eastern half of the island, had released nearly 32 megatons of carbon by October 19, more than any other year on record at that point in the year. “Emissions are already much higher than the 2015 total for the year, and it’s very likely that this will become the highest year on record for Papua New Guinea, even surpassing 1997,” said Guido van der Werf, a fire scientist at Wageningen University & Research. On the Indonesian side, sometimes called West New Guinea or Indonesian Papua, carbon emissions exceeded 35 megatons , the third highest after 2015 and 1997, other El Niño years with severe fires. Van der Werf led the development of GFED, a satellite-driven modeling framework that uses a mix of remote sensing , vegetation characteristics, and other information to estimate the extent of vegetation fires and the emissions over nearly three decades. Unusually dry weather—a byproduct of El Niño shifting rainfall patterns —has primed ecosystems across the island to burn. The southernmost part of Papua New Guinea, dominated by relatively fire-prone savannas and grasslands of the Trans-Fly region , went more than 90 consecutive days without rain, according to Papua New Guinea’s National Weather Service . Since August, parts of the region have seen precipitation of roughly 5 to 10 percent of normal, according to the weather service’s data. Local news outlets report that drought is causing crop failures , water shortages , and school disruptions . In this normally wet part of the world, people ignite the vast majority of fires, researchers say. Crop fires, pasture maintenance, deforestation and land clearing, and hunting are all common reasons people burn in New Guinea. In dry conditions, managed fires sometimes spread and burn uncontrolled as wildfires, particularly in the drier, southernmost parts of the island. “We’re seeing an exceptionally high level of fire activity in Papua New Guinea and Eastern Indonesia, particularly Indonesian Papua and Kalimantan, this year compared with Sumatra and other parts of Western Indonesia,” said Yang Chen, an associate researcher at the University of California, Irvine. “Papua has emerged as Indonesia’s new deforestation frontier.” Over the past two decades , land in Indonesian Papua has been cleared for industrial oil palm and pulpwood plantations, shifting small-scale cultivation, urban expansion, and mining . According to Global Forest Watch, the region lost 27,000 hectares of primary forest in 2025, nearly double the 2024 total and the most since 2017. Sumatra’s fires are relatively low compared to other drought years partly because many areas are already developed. “Areas with large oil palm, sugarcane, or pulpwood plantations also often have their own private fire brigades to protect their assets,” said Field. “It’s in unmanaged areas or primary forest edges where we’re generally seeing the most fire.” Researchers expect the fires to continue until the heavy rains of the wet season arrive in the southern part of New Guinea, typically in early November. item.title: Over 100 Ogun students hospitalised after suspected gas emissions
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta More than 100 students from several secondary schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo areas of Ogun State were reportedly hospitalised on Wednesday following another suspected gas emission that left students and staff struggling to breathe, with some fainting. The affected students were taken to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode, the General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo, and other healthcare facilities for medical attention. Among the schools reportedly affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, and Itamerin Comprehensive High School, Ago-Iwoye. A video circulating on social media showed some students fainting and being rushed for medical attention as panic spread across the affected communities. The incident has renewed concerns over recurring gaseous emissions in parts of Ijebu land, with residents and school authorities calling on the state government to establish the source and prevent further exposure. A teacher in one of the affected schools, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the incident began at about 10 a.m., when students and staff started experiencing breathing difficulties. “The students and staff started inhaling the gas and began to have difficulty breathing. Some of them fainted and had to be rushed to hospitals,” the teacher said. According to the teacher, some schools in Ago-Iwoye were forced to close for the day at about 11 a.m. as the situation worsened. “Some of the schools in Ago-Iwoye had to close for the day when the situation became frightening and unbearable. The worst-hit schools include Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School and Anglican Girls Grammar School in Ijebu-Ode,” the teacher added. The teacher said parents who heard about the incident rushed to their children’s schools to take them home amid fears for their safety. The teacher further claimed that similar emissions had occurred since April, sending hundreds of students to hospitals during previous incidents. “We are all worried about our health and the safety of our students. I think it is taking the government too long to get to the root of this mysterious gas emission. The government needs to act quickly before the situation gets worse,” the teacher said. Wednesday’s incident was reportedly the fourth occurrence of gaseous emissions disrupting school activities in Ijebu land since April 2026. The first reported incident in April affected about 40 students, while more than 120 students were reportedly hospitalised following another exposure in May. Another 69 students were reportedly hospitalised on June 1. Schools affected in previous incidents included Our Lady of Apostles Secondary School, Epe Garage, Ijebu-Ode; Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode; and St Anthony Grammar School, Ijebu-Imusin. The repeated incidents have heightened concerns about the safety of students and staff, particularly as some of the affected schools appear to have experienced multiple occurrences. Government
item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta More than 100 students from several secondary schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo areas of Ogun State were reportedly hospitalised on Wednesday following another suspected gas emission that left students and staff struggling to breathe, with some fainting. The affected students were taken to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode, the General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo, and other healthcare facilities for medical attention. Among the schools reportedly affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, and Itamerin Comprehensive High School, Ago-Iwoye. A video circulating on social media showed some students fainting and being rushed for medical attention as panic spread across the affected communities. The incident has renewed concerns over recurring gaseous emissions in parts of Ijebu land, with residents and school authorities calling on the state government to establish the source and prevent further exposure. A teacher in one of the affected schools, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the incident began at about 10 a.m., when students and staff started experiencing breathing difficulties. “The students and staff started inhaling the gas and began to have difficulty breathing. Some of them fainted and had to be rushed to hospitals,” the teacher said. According to the teacher, some schools in Ago-Iwoye were forced to close for the day at about 11 a.m. as the situation worsened. “Some of the schools in Ago-Iwoye had to close for the day when the situation became frightening and unbearable. The worst-hit schools include Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School and Anglican Girls Grammar School in Ijebu-Ode,” the teacher added. The teacher said parents who heard about the incident rushed to their children’s schools to take them home amid fears for their safety. The teacher further claimed that similar emissions had occurred since April, sending hundreds of students to hospitals during previous incidents. “We are all worried about our health and the safety of our students. I think it is taking the government too long to get to the root of this mysterious gas emission. The government needs to act quickly before the situation gets worse,” the teacher said. Wednesday’s incident was reportedly the fourth occurrence of gaseous emissions disrupting school activities in Ijebu land since April 2026. The first reported incident in April affected about 40 students, while more than 120 students were reportedly hospitalised following another exposure in May. Another 69 students were reportedly hospitalised on June 1. Schools affected in previous incidents included Our Lady of Apostles Secondary School, Epe Garage, Ijebu-Ode; Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode; and St Anthony Grammar School, Ijebu-Imusin. The repeated incidents have heightened concerns about the safety of students and staff, particularly as some of the affected schools appear to have experienced multiple occurrences. Government investigates suspected emissions Following previous incidents, Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, said the state government was working with relevant agencies and experts to determine the cause of the emissions. The governor said the Ministries of Environment and Health were collaborating with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority and the Department of Geology at Olabisi Onabanjo University to investigate the phenomenon. Abiodun, who spoke on the matter in June, said gas analysers had been installed in affected schools to establish the nature and concentration of the emissions. “Twice now, we have recorded cases of pollution in this school and some neighbouring schools. What is interesting is that the gas pollution occurred at about the same time in the affected schools — about three schools altogether — and this has happened on two separate occasions,” the governor said. He added that the gas detected during the investigation had been identified as methane. “Following the first occurrence, we installed gas analysers across the schools to determine the nature and concentration of the gas, which has now been confirmed to be methane,” he said. According to the governor, preliminary findings suggested that geological factors, including fault lines, could be responsible for the emissions. “Preliminary findings suggest there may be geological factors involved, possibly fault lines common to these locations, which could be responsible for the emissions. We are awaiting the final report from the professionals handling the investigation,” Abiodun said. When contacted on Wednesday, the state Commissioner for Environment, Ola Oresanya, said the government was monitoring the situation. “We are on top of the situation,” he said. Also speaking on the latest incident, Kehinde Bello, Senior Special Assistant to the governor and General Manager of the Ogun State Environmental Agency, said the emissions were linked to underground gas occurrences previously recorded in Ijebu-Ode since April. Bello, who visited affected areas in Ijebu-Ode and Ijebu-Igbo to assess the situation, said the government was working towards finding a lasting solution. He said investigations had indicated that the phenomenon could be a natural occurrence associated with geological and tectonic fault lines, rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak. Bello urged residents to remain calm, assuring them that the affected students were expected to recover after receiving medical attention. He also advised residents exposed to the odour to cover their noses and mouths with wet handkerchiefs rather than wear nose masks. However, the precise source of the emissions and the reasons for their recurrence remain unclear, with residents awaiting the outcome of the investigation. As of the time of filing this report, medical personnel were reportedly attending to affected students at general hospitals and other healthcare facilities. The latest incident has intensified calls for a conclusive investigation and effective preventive measures to protect students and staff from further exposure.
